title.zh: 卷六 齊本紀上第六: 高祖神武帝 世宗文襄帝
title.en: Volume 6 Northern Qi Annals 1: Emperor Gaozu Shenwu, Emperor Shizong Wenxiang
title.raw: 卷六 齊本紀上第六: 高祖神武帝 世宗文襄帝 Volume 6 Northern Qi Annals 1: Emperor Gaozu Shenwu, Emperor Shizong Wenxiang

sentences.zh: 高祖神武帝 世宗文襄帝

translations.literal: Gaozu Emperor Shenwu; Shizong Emperor Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu the Divine Martial; Emperor Shizong the Cultured and Assisting.

sentences.zh: 齊高祖神武皇帝姓高氏，諱歡，字賀六渾，勃海蓚人也。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor Gaozu of Qi, surname Gao, taboo name Huan, courtesy name Heliuhun, was a native of Lou in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's founding Emperor Shenwu, of the Gao clan, bore the taboo name Huan and the courtesy name Heliuhun; he came from Lou in Bohai commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖隱，晉玄菟太守。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yin was Governor of Mystic Hare under the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, his forebear Yin had served the Jin as governor of Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 隱生慶，慶生泰，泰生湖，三世仕慕容氏。

translations.literal: Yin begot Qing; Qing begot Tai; Tai begot Hu; for three generations they served the Murong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin fathered Qing, Qing fathered Tai, and Tai fathered Hu; all three generations held office under the Murong.

sentences.zh: 及慕容寶敗，國亂。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao was defeated, the state fell into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao met defeat, the realm dissolved into chaos.

sentences.zh: 湖率眾歸魏，為右將軍。

translations.literal: Hu led his followers in submission to Wei and became General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Hu brought his men over to Wei and was made General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 湖生四子。

translations.literal: Hu had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hu had four sons.

sentences.zh: 第三子謐，仕魏，位至侍御史，坐法徙居懷朔鎮。

translations.literal: The third son Mi served Wei, rose to Attending Censor, and was banished to Huai-shuo garrison for a legal offense.
translations.idiomatic: The third son, Mi, entered Wei service and reached Attending Censor before he was exiled to Huai-shuo garrison for breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 謐生皇考樹生，性通率，不事家業。

translations.literal: Mi begot the late Emperor's father Shusheng, who was open and unceremonious and did not attend to family business.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fathered the late emperor's father Shusheng, a man of blunt, easy manners who cared nothing for household affairs.

sentences.zh: 住居白道南，數有赤光紫氣之異。

translations.literal: He lived south of White Road, and red light and purple vapor appeared there several times.
translations.idiomatic: His home lay south of White Road, where crimson light and purple mists were seen again and again.

sentences.zh: 鄰人以為怪，勸徙居以避之。

translations.literal: Neighbors thought it strange and urged him to move away to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors took it for an omen and urged him to move elsewhere and escape it.

sentences.zh: 皇考曰：「安知非吉？

translations.literal: The late Emperor's father said, "How do you know it is not auspicious?
translations.idiomatic: His father replied, "Who says this is not a blessing?

sentences.zh: 」居之自若。

translations.literal: " He remained there as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He stayed on without concern.

sentences.zh: 及神武生而皇妣韓氏殂，養於同產姊婿鎮獄隊尉景家。

translations.literal: When Shenwu was born the imperial mother Lady Han died; he was reared in the home of his uterine sister's husband Jing, captain of the garrison prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu was born; his mother Lady Han died at once, and he was raised in the household of his elder uterine sister's husband Jing, captain of the garrison prison.

sentences.zh: 神武既累世北邊，故習其俗，遂同鮮卑。

translations.literal: Shenwu, having lived on the northern frontier for generations, learned its ways and came to resemble the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Generations on the northern marches had taught him frontier ways, and he grew up almost as one of the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 長而深沈有大度，輕財重士，為豪俠所宗。

translations.literal: As he grew he was deep and reserved, with great breadth of mind; he prized men of talent over wealth and was looked up to by bold spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In manhood he was grave and far-seeing, open-handed with talent and light with money; men of daring spirit took him for their leader.

sentences.zh: 目有精光，長頭高權，齒白如玉，少有人傑表。

translations.literal: His eyes held a keen light; he had a long head and high cheekbones; his teeth were white as jade; in youth he bore the look of an uncommon man.
translations.idiomatic: His gaze was sharp, his skull long and his cheekbones high, his teeth white as jade; even young he had the bearing of one marked for greatness.

sentences.zh: 家貧，及娉武明皇后，始有馬，得給鎮為隊主。

translations.literal: His family was poor; only after he married Empress Wuming did he acquire a horse and was appointed squad leader in the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Poverty held the household until his marriage to Empress Wuming brought him his first horse and a post as squad leader at the garrison.

sentences.zh: 鎮將遼西段長常奇神武貌，謂曰：「君有康濟才，終不徒然。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Duan Chang of Liaoxi often marveled at Shenwu's appearance and said to him, "Sir, you have the talent to bring order to the age; you will not end as a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, the garrison commander, was struck by Shenwu's looks and told him, "You have what it takes to steady an age; you will not die obscure.

sentences.zh: 」便以子孫為托。

translations.literal: " He entrusted his sons and grandsons to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He entrusted his sons and grandsons to Shenwu's care.

sentences.zh: 及貴，追贈長司空，擢其子寧而用之。

translations.literal: When Shenwu rose to power he posthumously enfeoffed Chang as Minister of Works and promoted his son Ning to office.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shenwu had risen, he posthumously enfeoffed Duan Chang as Minister of Works and raised his son Ning to office.

sentences.zh: 神武自隊主轉為函使。

translations.literal: Shenwu advanced from squad leader to courier of the mail bags.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu rose from squad leader to courier of the sealed dispatches.

sentences.zh: 嘗乘驛過建興，雲務書晦，雷聲隨之，半日乃絕，若有神應者。

translations.literal: Once riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist veiled the sky in ink-darkness; thunder followed him and did not cease for half a day, as though spirits answered him.
translations.idiomatic: Once on post-horse through Jianxing, ink-dark clouds swallowed the sky and thunder rolled at his heels for half a day, as if heaven itself answered him.

sentences.zh: 每行道路，往來無風塵之色。

translations.literal: Whenever he walked the roads, no dust rose where he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he walked the road lay still, without a speck of dust.

sentences.zh: 又嘗夢履眾星而行，覺而內喜。

translations.literal: He also dreamed that he trod upon the stars as he walked; waking, he rejoiced inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed once that he walked upon the stars; waking, he was glad in his heart.

sentences.zh: 為函使六年，每至洛陽，給令史麻祥使。

translations.literal: For six years as courier, whenever he reached Luoyang he was assigned to the clerk Ma Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Six years as courier brought him to Luoyang again and again, each time under the clerk Ma Xiang.

sentences.zh: 祥嘗以肉啖神武。

translations.literal: Xiang once fed him meat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang once offered him meat to eat.

sentences.zh: 神武性不立食，坐而進之。

translations.literal: Shenwu would not eat standing; he sat to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu would not eat on his feet; he sat down to take the food.

sentences.zh: 祥以為慢己，笞神武四十。

translations.literal: Xiang took this as disrespect and had Shenwu flogged forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang read this as insolence and had Shenwu beaten forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 及自洛陽還，傾產以結客。

translations.literal: When he returned from Luoyang he poured out his property to win followers.
translations.idiomatic: Back from Luoyang, he spent his whole fortune gathering allies.

sentences.zh: 親故怪問之，答曰：「吾至洛陽，宿衛羽林相率焚領軍張彜宅，朝廷懼其亂而不問，為政若此，事可知也。

translations.literal: Kin and friends wondered and asked him; he answered, "When I reached Luoyang, the palace guards of the Feathered Forest together burned the residence of the Director of the Palace Domestics Zhang Yi, and the court, fearing disorder, did not punish them. When government runs so, the outcome is plain.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives marveled and asked why; he said, "In Luoyang the Feathered Forest guards together burned Director Zhang Yi's house, and the court, afraid of riot, let it pass. Rule like that tells you everything.

sentences.zh: 財物豈可常守邪？

translations.literal: Can wealth be hoarded forever?
translations.idiomatic: What use is wealth if you cling to it forever?

sentences.zh: 」自是乃有澄清天下之志。

translations.literal: " From then on he harbored the will to clarify all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " From that day he set his mind on clearing the realm.

sentences.zh: 與懷朔省事雲中司馬子如及秀容人劉貴、中山人賈顯智為奔走之友。

translations.literal: With Sima Ziru of Yunzhong, clerk for Huai-shuo affairs, and Liu Gui of Xiurong and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan he became sworn friends who ran his errands.
translations.idiomatic: He bound himself to Sima Ziru of Yunzhong, a Huai-shuo clerk, and to Liu Gui of Xiurong and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan as friends who would go anywhere at his call.

sentences.zh: 懷朔戶曹史孫騰、外兵史侯景亦相友結。

translations.literal: Sun Teng, clerk of the household register at Huai-shuo, and Hou Jing, clerk of external military affairs, also joined the circle.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng of the Huai-shuo household register and Hou Jing of the external military desk joined them as well.

sentences.zh: 劉貴嘗得一白鷹，與神武及尉景、蔡俊、子如、賈顯智等獵於沃野。

translations.literal: Liu Gui once obtained a white hawk; with Shenwu and Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi and others he hunted at Woye.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui once caught a white hawk; with Shenwu, Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, and Jia Xianzhi he hunted the wilds of Woye.

sentences.zh: 見一赤兔，每搏輙逸，遂至迥澤。

translations.literal: They saw a red hare; each time they closed it broke away, until they reached Jiong Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: A red hare appeared; every chase ended in escape, until they came to Jiong Marsh.

sentences.zh: 澤中有茅屋，將奔入，有狗自屋中出噬之，鷹兔俱死。

translations.literal: In the marsh was a thatched hut; as the hare ran to enter, a dog rushed from the hut and bit it; hawk and hare both died.
translations.idiomatic: A hut stood in the marsh; the hare bolted for it, but a dog burst out and killed it, and hawk and hare died together.

sentences.zh: 神武怒，以鳴鏑射之，狗斃。

translations.literal: Shenwu in anger shot it with a whistling arrow; the dog fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu in fury loosed a whistling arrow and dropped the dog.

sentences.zh: 屋中乃有二人出，持神武襟甚急。

translations.literal: Two men came out of the hut and seized Shenwu's collar very hard.
translations.idiomatic: Two men came out and seized Shenwu by the collar with sudden force.

sentences.zh: 其母兩目盲，曳杖，呵其二子，曰：「何故觸大家！

translations.literal: Their mother, blind in both eyes, dragged her staff and scolded her two sons, saying, "Why do you touch the great lord!
translations.idiomatic: Their mother, blind in both eyes, hobbled forward on her staff and cried at her sons, "How dare you lay hands on the great lord!

sentences.zh: 出甕中酒，烹羊以待客。

translations.literal: She brought wine from a jar and slaughtered a sheep to entertain the guests.
translations.idiomatic: She drew wine from the jar and killed a sheep to feast them.

sentences.zh: 因自言善暗相，遍捫諸人，言皆貴，而指麾俱由神武。

translations.literal: She said of herself that she was skilled in secret physiognomy; she felt all of them over and declared each noble, and that all would rise by Shenwu's hand.
translations.idiomatic: She claimed skill in hidden physiognomy, passed her hands over each man and called every one destined for rank, all to rise through Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「子如歷位顯，智不善終。

translations.literal: She also said, "Ziru will reach high office; Zhi will not end well.
translations.idiomatic: She added, "Ziru will rise high; Zhi will come to no good end.

sentences.zh: 」飲竟，出行數里，還更訪之。

translations.literal: " When the drinking was done they went out several li, then turned back to visit again.
translations.idiomatic: " When the cups were empty they rode on for miles, then turned back to call again.

sentences.zh: 則本無人居，乃向非人也。

translations.literal: There was no one living there at all; those they had met were not human.
translations.idiomatic: No one lived there at all; what they had met was not of this world.

sentences.zh: 由是諸人益加敬異。

translations.literal: From this the company honored and marveled at him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: After that his companions revered him still more deeply.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，柔玄鎮人杜洛周反於上谷，神武乃與同志從之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, Du Luozhou of Rouxuan garrison rebelled at Shanggu; Shenwu and his comrades followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang year one Du Luozhou of Rouxuan garrison rose at Shanggu, and Shenwu and his friends went with him.

sentences.zh: 醜其行事，私與尉景、段榮、蔡俊圖之，不果而逃，為其騎所追。

translations.literal: He detested Luozhou's conduct; in secret with Jing, Duan Rong, and Cai Jun he plotted against him; the plot failed and he fled; Luozhou's horsemen pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: He loathed Luozhou's ways; with Jing, Duan Rong, and Cai Jun he plotted in secret, failed, and fled while Luozhou's riders gave chase.

sentences.zh: 文襄及魏永熙後皆幼，武明後於牛上抱負之。

translations.literal: Wenxiang and the Yongxi empress were still young; Empress Wuming carried them on her back upon the ox.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang and the Yongxi empress were still infants; Empress Wuming bore them on her back upon the ox.

sentences.zh: 文襄屢落牛，神武彎弓將射之以決去，後呼榮求救，賴榮透下取之以免。

translations.literal: Wenxiang fell from the ox again and again; Shenwu bent his bow to shoot him and settle whether they should leave him; the empress called on Rong to save him, and thanks to Rong, who reached down and pulled him off, he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang kept slipping from the ox; Shenwu strung his bow as if to shoot the boy and decide the matter; the empress cried to Rong, who leaned down and snatched the child up in time.

sentences.zh: 遂奔葛榮，又亡歸爾朱榮於秀容。

translations.literal: He then fled to Ge Rong, and fled again to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: He fled next to Ge Rong, then broke away again and sought Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 先是劉貴事榮，盛言神武美，至是始得見。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Gui had served Rong and spoken much of Shenwu's excellence; only then did he obtain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui had long served Rong and praised Shenwu; only now did Shenwu win an audience.

sentences.zh: 以憔悴故，未之奇也。

translations.literal: Because of his haggard appearance Rong did not find him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: His worn, travel-stained look left Rong unimpressed.

sentences.zh: 貴乃為神武更衣，復求見焉。

translations.literal: Gui then had Shenwu change clothes and sought another audience.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had him dress anew and asked for another meeting.

sentences.zh: 因隨榮之廄，廄有惡馬，榮命剪之，神武乃不加羈絆而剪，竟不蹄嚙。

translations.literal: He then followed Rong to the stables; there was a vicious horse, and Rong ordered its mane cut; Shenwu did not bind it yet cut it, and it never kicked or bit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Rong to the stables, where a savage horse waited; Rong ordered its mane trimmed; Shenwu cut it without tying the beast, and it never struck or bit.

sentences.zh: 已而起曰：「禦惡人亦如此馬矣。

translations.literal: When he had finished he rose and said, "Taming wicked men is like this horse.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished he said, "Breaking wicked men is like breaking this horse.

sentences.zh: 」榮遂坐神武於床下，屏左右而訪時事。

translations.literal: " Rong then seated Shenwu below his couch, dismissed those nearby, and questioned him on the times.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong set him below the couch, sent attendants away, and questioned him on affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「聞公有馬十二谷，色別為群，將此竟何用也？」

translations.literal: Shenwu said, "I hear that my lord has twelve valleys of horses, each color a separate herd; what use is all this meant to serve?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "They say you keep twelve valleys of horses, color sorted into herds; what do you mean to do with them?"

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「但言爾意。

translations.literal: Rong said, "Speak only your own mind.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Say what you yourself intend.

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「方今天子愚弱，太后淫亂，孽寵擅命，朝政不行。

translations.literal: " Shenwu said, "Today the Son of Heaven is foolish and weak, the empress dowager dissolute, favored minions seize command, and court policy cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenwu said, "The Son of Heaven is weak and dull, the empress dowager corrupt, minions hold the reins, and nothing sound comes from court.

sentences.zh: 以明公雄武，乘時奮發，討鄭儼、徐紇而清帝側，霸業可舉鞭而成。

translations.literal: With my lord's martial valor, if you seize the moment and strike, punish Zheng Yan and Xu Chi and clear the emperor's side, hegemony can be achieved with a flick of the whip.
translations.idiomatic: With your valor, if you rise now, cut down Zheng Yan and Xu Chi, and cleanse the emperor's flank, empire is yours for a lifted whip.

sentences.zh: 此賀六渾之意也。

translations.literal: This is the intent of Heliuhun.
translations.idiomatic: That is what Heliuhun would do.

sentences.zh: 」榮大悅，語自日中至夜半乃出。

translations.literal: " Rong was greatly pleased; they talked from midday until midnight before he left.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong was delighted; they talked from noon deep into night before Shenwu left.

sentences.zh: 自是每參軍謀。

translations.literal: From then on he took part in every military council.
translations.idiomatic: After that he sat in on every council of war.

sentences.zh: 後從榮徙據并州，抵揚州邑人龐蒼鷹，止圍焦中。

translations.literal: Later he followed Rong in moving to hold Bing province and lodged with Pang Cangying of Yangzhou, stopping in the round walled compound.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Rong to Bing province and lodged with Pang Cangying of Yangzhou in the round walled compound.

sentences.zh: 每從外歸，主人遙聞行響動地。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned from outside, his host heard his tread shake the ground from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came in from outside, his host heard footsteps that shook the earth from far off.

sentences.zh: 蒼鷹母數見圍焦，上赤氣赫然屬天。

translations.literal: Cangying's mother several times saw the round compound wreathed in red vapor reaching to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cangying's mother often saw red vapor crown the compound and climb to the sky.

sentences.zh: 又蒼鷹嘗夜欲入，有青衣人拔刀叱曰：「何故觸王？

translations.literal: Cangying also tried to enter by night; a man in green drew a blade and shouted, "Why do you touch the king?
translations.idiomatic: Cangying tried to enter one night; a man in green pulled a sword and cried, "Why do you trouble the king?

sentences.zh: 」言訖不見。

translations.literal: When the words ended he was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: The voice ceased and the figure was gone.

sentences.zh: 始以為異，密覘之。

translations.literal: At first he thought it strange and watched in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He took it for a marvel and watched in secret.

sentences.zh: 唯見赤蛇蟠床上，乃益驚異。

translations.literal: He saw only a red serpent coiled on the bed, and marveled all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He saw only a red serpent coiled on the bed, and wondered the more.

sentences.zh: 因殺牛分肉，厚以相奉。

translations.literal: He therefore slaughtered an ox and divided the meat, sending a generous share.
translations.idiomatic: He killed an ox, divided the meat, and sent Shenwu a generous portion.

sentences.zh: 蒼鷹母求以神武為義子。

translations.literal: Cangying's mother asked to adopt Shenwu as a son by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Cangying's mother asked to take Shenwu as a ritual son.

sentences.zh: 及得志，以其宅為第，號為南宅。

translations.literal: When he had achieved his aim he made that house his mansion and called it the Southern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: When power was his, he made that house his mansion and called it the Southern Residence.

sentences.zh: 雖門巷開廣，堂宇崇麗，其本所住團焦，以石堊塗之，留而不毀。

translations.literal: Though the gates and lanes were broad and the halls lofty, the original round compound where he had lived he coated with lime and plaster and left undestroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Though his gates ran wide and his halls stood tall, the old round compound where he had lived he whitewashed with lime and left standing.

sentences.zh: 至文宣時，遂為宮。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wenxuan it became part of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wenxuan it became part of the palace.

sentences.zh: 既而榮以神武為親信都督。

translations.literal: Then Rong made Shenwu trusted commander.
translations.idiomatic: Then Rong named him trusted commander.

sentences.zh: 於時魏明帝銜鄭儼、徐紇，逼靈太后。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming of Wei resented Zheng Yan and Xu Chi and pressed the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Ming of Wei hated Zheng Yan and Xu Chi and pressed the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 未敢制，私使榮舉兵內向。

translations.literal: He did not dare move against them openly and secretly ordered Rong to raise troops and march inward.
translations.idiomatic: He dared not move openly and secretly ordered Rong to march inward with an army.

sentences.zh: 榮以神武為前鋒。

translations.literal: Rong made Shenwu vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Rong put Shenwu in the van.

sentences.zh: 至上黨，明帝又私詔停之。

translations.literal: When they reached Shangdang, Ming again sent a secret edict halting them.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangdang, Ming again sent a secret order to halt.

sentences.zh: 及帝暴崩，榮遂入洛。

translations.literal: When the emperor died suddenly, Rong entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died suddenly, Rong entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 因將篡位，神武諫恐不聽，請鑄像卜之。

translations.literal: He was about to seize the throne; Shenwu remonstrated, fearing he would not listen, and asked to cast an image and divine by it.
translations.idiomatic: He was set to usurp the throne; Shenwu urged caution, fearing he would not listen, and asked to cast an image and divine the omen.

sentences.zh: 鑄不成，乃止。

translations.literal: The casting would not succeed, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The casting failed, and Rong abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 孝莊帝立，以定策勛，封銅鞮伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned; for fixing the succession Shenwu was enfeoffed as Baron of Tongdi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang took the throne; for helping settle the succession Shenwu was made Baron of Tongdi.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱榮擊葛榮，令神武喻下賊別稱王者七人。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong attacked Ge Rong he had Shenwu persuade seven rebel leaders who styled themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong struck Ge Rong he sent Shenwu to win over seven rebel chiefs who called themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 後與行臺於暉破羊侃於太山。

translations.literal: Later with the Mobile Secretariat Yu Hui he defeated Yang Kan on Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Yu Hui of the Mobile Secretariat, he broke Yang Kan on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 尋與元天穆破邢杲於濟南。

translations.literal: Soon after, with Yuan Tianmu he defeated Xing Gao at Ji'nan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, with Yuan Tianmu, he defeated Xing Gao at Ji'nan.

sentences.zh: 累遷第三鎮人酋長。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to chieftain of the third garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to chieftain of the third garrison.

sentences.zh: 嘗在榮帳內，榮嘗問左右曰：「一日無我，誰可主軍？

translations.literal: Once in Rong's tent, Rong asked those beside him, "One day without me, who could command the army?
translations.idiomatic: Once in Rong's tent Rong asked his staff, "If I were gone a day, who could lead this host?

sentences.zh: 」皆稱爾朱兆。

translations.literal: " All named Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: " All named Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「此正可統三千騎以還。

translations.literal: Rong said, "He is fit to lead three thousand horse back home.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "He is fit to lead three thousand horse home again.

sentences.zh: 堪代我主眾者，唯賀六渾耳。

translations.literal: Only Heliuhun could replace me in commanding the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Only Heliuhun could stand in my place over the whole host.

sentences.zh: 」因誡兆曰：「爾非其匹，終當為其子穿鼻。

translations.literal: " He then warned Zhao, "You are not his match; in the end his son will pierce your nose.
translations.idiomatic: " He warned Zhao, "You are not his equal; in the end his son will run a rope through your nose.

sentences.zh: 」乃以神武為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: " He then made Shenwu Governor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made Shenwu governor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 於是大聚斂，因劉貴貨榮下要人，盡得其意。

translations.literal: Thereupon he amassed wealth on a great scale; through Liu Gui he bribed Rong's chief men and learned all their minds.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered wealth on a vast scale; through Liu Gui he bought Rong's inner circle and learned every mind there.

sentences.zh: 時州庫角無故自鳴，神武異之，無幾而孝莊誅榮。

translations.literal: At that time the horn in the provincial treasury sounded of itself without cause; Shenwu thought it strange; before long Xiaozhuang executed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The state horn in the treasury sounded by itself; Shenwu took it for a sign; soon Xiaozhuang killed Rong.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱兆自晉陽將舉兵赴洛，召神武。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao was about to raise troops from Jinyang and march on Luoyang he summoned Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao prepared to march from Jinyang on Luoyang he summoned Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武使長史孫騰辭以絳蜀、汾胡欲反，不可委去。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent his chief clerk Sun Teng to plead that the Jiang and Fen barbarians were on the verge of revolt and he could not leave his post.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sent his chief clerk Sun Teng to plead that Jiang and Fen barbarians were about to rise and he could not abandon his post.

sentences.zh: 兆恨焉。

translations.literal: Zhao hated this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was furious.

sentences.zh: 騰復命，神武曰：「兆舉兵犯上，此大賊也，吾不能久事之。」

translations.literal: Teng returned with the answer; Shenwu said, "Zhao is raising troops to violate his sovereign; he is a great rebel; I cannot serve him long."
translations.idiomatic: When Teng returned, Shenwu said, "Zhao marches against his lord; that is treason on the largest scale, and I cannot follow him much longer."

sentences.zh: 自是始有圖兆計。

translations.literal: From then on he began to plot against Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment he began plotting Zhao's downfall.

sentences.zh: 及兆入洛，執莊帝以北。

translations.literal: When Zhao entered Luoyang he seized Emperor Zhuang and took him north.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao entered Luoyang he seized Emperor Zhuang and dragged him north.

sentences.zh: 神武聞之大驚。

translations.literal: Shenwu was greatly shocked when he heard it.
translations.idiomatic: The news struck Shenwu like a blow.

sentences.zh: 又使孫騰偽賀兆，因密覘孝莊所在，將劫以舉義，不果。

translations.literal: He also sent Sun Teng to offer false congratulations to Zhao and secretly spy out where Xiaozhuang was held, intending to seize him and raise the standard of righteousness; it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Sun Teng to feign congratulations while secretly learning where Xiaozhuang was held, planning to snatch the emperor and raise the righteous banner; the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 乃以書喻之，言不宜執天子以受惡名於海內。

translations.literal: He then wrote to advise Zhao that he ought not hold the Son of Heaven and earn a wicked name throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote urging Zhao not to hold the Son of Heaven and win infamy across the realm.

sentences.zh: 兆不納，殺帝而與爾朱世隆等立長廣王曄。

translations.literal: Zhao did not accept it; he killed the emperor and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned the Prince of Changguang, Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao refused; he killed the emperor and with Shilong and others set up the Prince of Changguang, Ye.

sentences.zh: 改元建明，封神武為平陽郡公。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Jianming, and Shenwu was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The era was renamed Jianming, and Shenwu was made Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 及費也頭紇豆陵步籓入秀容，逼晉陽，兆征神武。

translations.literal: When the Feiyetou chieftain Hedouling Buban of the He tribe entered Xiurong and pressed Jinyang, Zhao summoned Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Buban of the Feiyetou He entered Xiurong and threatened Jinyang, Zhao summoned Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武將往，賀拔焉過兒請緩行以弊之。

translations.literal: As Shenwu was about to go, Heba Yaguor urged him to delay and wear the enemy down.
translations.idiomatic: As Shenwu prepared to march, Heba Yaguor urged delay to exhaust the foe.

sentences.zh: 神武乃往逗留，辭以河無橋，不得渡。

translations.literal: Shenwu therefore went but lingered, pleading that the river had no bridge and he could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu went but lingered, claiming the river had no bridge and he could not cross.

sentences.zh: 步籓軍盛，敗走。

translations.literal: Bupan's army was strong but was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bupan's host was strong but broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 初，孝莊之誅爾朱榮，知其黨必有逆謀，乃密敕步籓，令襲其後。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiaozhuang executed Erzhu Rong, knowing his faction would surely rebel, he had secretly ordered Buban to strike them from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang killed Rong he knew the clan would rebel and secretly ordered Buban to strike from behind.

sentences.zh: 步籓既敗兆等，以兵勢日盛，兆又請救於神武。

translations.literal: After Buban had defeated Zhao and the others, as his forces grew daily stronger, Zhao again asked Shenwu for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: After Buban beat Zhao, his strength swelled daily, and Zhao again begged Shenwu for aid.

sentences.zh: 神武內圖兆，復慮步籓後之難除，乃與兆悉力破之，籓死。

translations.literal: Shenwu plotted against Zhao inwardly yet feared Buban would be hard to remove afterward; he therefore joined Zhao with full force and destroyed him; Buban died.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu plotted against Zhao inwardly yet feared Buban would be hard to root out later; he joined Zhao with full force and destroyed him; Buban died.

sentences.zh: 深德神武，誓為兄弟。

translations.literal: Zhao was deeply grateful to Shenwu and swore brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao owed Shenwu a deep debt and swore brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 時世隆、度律、彥伯共執朝政，天光據關右，兆據并州。

translations.literal: At that time Shilong, Dulü, and Yanbo together held court power; Tianguang held the passes west; Zhao held Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong, Dulü, and Yanbo held court; Tianguang held the western passes; Zhao held Bing.

sentences.zh: 仲遠據東郡，各擁兵為暴，天下苦之。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan held Dong commandery; each hoarded troops and acted as tyrants, and the realm suffered under them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan held Dongjun; each hoarded armies and ravaged the land, and the realm groaned.

sentences.zh: 葛榮眾流入並、肆者二十餘萬，為契胡陵暴，皆不聊生。

translations.literal: More than two hundred thousand of Ge Rong's followers had flowed into Bing and Si; the Toba bullied them cruelly and none could live.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand of Ge Rong's men had poured into Bing and Si; the Toba oppressed them until life was unbearable.

sentences.zh: 大小二十六反，誅夷者半，猶草竊不止。

translations.literal: Twenty-six uprisings large and small broke out; half were slaughtered in punishment, yet banditry still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six revolts rose large and small; half the people were killed in reprisal, yet banditry never ceased.

sentences.zh: 兆患之，問計於神武。

translations.literal: Zhao was troubled by this and asked Shenwu for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was at his wits' end and asked Shenwu for counsel.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「六鎮反殘，不可盡殺，宜選王素腹心者，私使統焉。

translations.literal: Shenwu said, "The rebels of the six garrisons cannot all be killed; you should choose men of royal blood whom you trust and secretly set them to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "The six-garrison rebels cannot all be killed; choose princes you trust and set them secretly to command them.

sentences.zh: 若有犯者，罪其帥，則所罪者寡。

translations.literal: If there are offenders, punish their commanders, and few will be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Punish the commander when men offend, and few need die.

sentences.zh: 」兆曰：「善！

translations.literal: Zhao said, "Good!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Good!

sentences.zh: 誰可行也？

translations.literal: Who can carry this out?"
translations.idiomatic: Who can do it?"

sentences.zh: 」賀拔允時在坐，請神武。

translations.literal: Heba Yun was then present and nominated Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yun sat by and named Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武拳毆之，折其一齒，曰：「生平天柱時，奴輩伏處分如鷹犬。

translations.literal: Shenwu struck him with his fist and broke one tooth, saying, "In the days of the pillar Tianzhu, you slaves lay under orders like hawks and hounds.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu punched him and broke a tooth, crying, "When the pillar Tianzhu lived, you slaves crouched under orders like hawks and hounds.

sentences.zh: 今日天下安置在王，而阿鞠泥敢誣下罔上，請殺之。」

translations.literal: Today the realm is settled on the king, yet you Aju-ni dare deceive those below and cheat those above; I ask that he be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm rests on the king, yet you Aju-ni dare lie up and down the ranks; kill him."

sentences.zh: 兆以神武為誠，遂以委焉。

translations.literal: Zhao took Shenwu for sincere and entrusted the task to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao took Shenwu for loyal and gave him the command.

sentences.zh: 神武以兆醉，恐醒後或致疑貳，遂出，宣言：「受委統州鎮兵，可集汾東受令。

translations.literal: Shenwu feared that when Zhao sobered he might grow suspicious, so he went out and proclaimed, "I have received orders to command the garrison troops of the province; assemble east of the Fen to receive commands."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zhao would sober and doubt him, Shenwu went out and proclaimed, "I am commissioned to command the provincial garrisons; gather east of the Fen for orders."

sentences.zh: 」乃建牙陽曲川，陳部分。

translations.literal: He then raised his standard at Yangqu River and set out the divisions.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his standard at Yangqu River and arrayed the divisions.

sentences.zh: 有款軍門者，絳巾袍，自稱梗楊驛子，願廁左右。

translations.literal: One who came sincerely to the camp wore a red headcloth and robe, called himself the courier of Gengyang station, and asked to serve at his side.
translations.idiomatic: A man came to camp in red headcloth and robe, called himself the Gengyang courier, and begged to serve at his side.

sentences.zh: 訪之，則以力聞，嘗於并州市搤殺人者，乃署為親信。

translations.literal: Asked about him, he was known for strength; he had once strangled a man in Bingzhou market; Shenwu appointed him as a trusted follower.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry showed him famed for strength; he had once strangled a man in the Bingzhou market; Shenwu made him a trusted follower.

sentences.zh: 兵士素惡兆而樂神武，於是莫不皆至。

translations.literal: The soldiers had long hated Zhao and rejoiced in Shenwu; none failed to come.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers hated Zhao and loved Shenwu; none failed to come.

sentences.zh: 居無何，又使劉貴請兆。

translations.literal: Before long he again sent Liu Gui to request Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he sent Liu Gui to summon Zhao again.

sentences.zh: 以並、肆頻歲霜旱，降戶掘黃鼠而食之，皆面無谷色，徒汙人國土。

translations.literal: Because Bing and Si had suffered frost and drought for years, the surrendered households dug yellow rats to eat and all had faces without the color of grain; they only fouled the state's soil.
translations.idiomatic: Bing and Si had known frost and drought for years; surrendered households ate yellow rats and starved white; they only fouled the realm.

sentences.zh: 請令就食山東，待溫飽而處分之。

translations.literal: He asked that they be sent to eat in Shandong and be dealt with after they were fed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to send them east to Shandong to eat and settle them once they were full.

sentences.zh: 兆從其議。

translations.literal: Zhao followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao agreed.

sentences.zh: 其長史慕容紹宗諫曰：「不可，今四方擾擾，人懷異望，況高公雄略，又握大兵，將不可為。

translations.literal: His chief clerk Murong Shaozong remonstrated, saying, "You must not; now the four quarters are in turmoil and men harbor other hopes; moreover the Duke of Gao is heroic in strategy and holds a great army; this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Murong Shaozong warned, "Do not; the realm is in turmoil and hearts waver; Gao is bold in counsel and holds a great army; this cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 」兆曰：「香火重誓，何所慮邪？

translations.literal: Zhao said, "We have sworn a heavy oath over incense; what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "We swore a heavy oath over incense; what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」紹宗曰：「親兄弟尚難信，何論香火！

translations.literal: Shaozong said, "Even full brothers are hard to trust; how much less incense oaths!"
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong said, "Even blood brothers are hard to trust; how much less incense oaths!"

sentences.zh: 」時兆左右已受神武金，因譖紹宗與神武舊隙，兆乃禁紹宗而催神武發。

translations.literal: By then those at Zhao's side had already taken Shenwu's gold; they slandered Shaozong as having old enmity with Shenwu; Zhao imprisoned Shaozong and urged Shenwu to march.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhao's men had taken Shenwu's gold; they slandered Shaozong for old grudges with Shenwu; Zhao jailed Shaozong and pressed Shenwu to march.

sentences.zh: 神武乃自晉陽出滏口。

translations.literal: Shenwu then marched out of Jinyang through Fukou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu marched out of Jinyang through Fukou.

sentences.zh: 路逢爾朱榮妻鄉郡長公主自洛陽來，馬三百匹，盡奪易之。

translations.literal: On the road he met the Princess of Xiangjun, Rong's wife, coming from Luoyang with three hundred horses; he seized them all and exchanged mounts.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met Princess Xiangjun, Rong's wife, coming from Luoyang with three hundred horses; he seized them all.

sentences.zh: 兆聞，乃釋紹宗而問焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao heard of it he released Shaozong and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao heard, he freed Shaozong and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 紹宗曰：「猶掌握中物也。

translations.literal: Shaozong said, "He is still something in the palm of your hand."
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong said, "He is still something in the palm of your hand."

sentences.zh: 」於是自追神武，至襄垣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he himself pursued Shenwu and reached Xiangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rode after Shenwu himself and reached Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 會漳水暴長，橋壞。

translations.literal: The Zhang River rose in flood and the bridge was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang River rose in flood and broke the bridge.

sentences.zh: 神武隔水拜曰：「所以借公主馬，非有他故，備山東盜耳。

translations.literal: Shenwu bowed across the water and said, "The reason I borrowed the princess's horses was not for any other cause but to guard against bandits in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu bowed across the water and said, "I borrowed the princess's horses only to guard against Shandong bandits.

sentences.zh: 王受公主言，自來賜追，今渡河而死，不辭，此眾便叛。

translations.literal: The king, accepting the princess's words, came in person to pursue me; if I cross the river now I die without regret, but this host will rebel at once."
translations.idiomatic: You believed the princess and came yourself to pursue me; cross the river and I die gladly, but this host will rebel at once."

sentences.zh: 」兆自陳無此意，因輕馬渡，與神武坐幕下，陳謝，遂授刀引頭，使神武斫己。

translations.literal: Zhao declared he had no such intent; he crossed lightly on horseback, sat with Shenwu beneath the tent, apologized, then handed over his sword and offered his neck for Shenwu to strike him down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao swore he meant no harm; he crossed lightly, sat with Shenwu beneath the tent, apologized, handed over his sword, and offered his neck.

sentences.zh: 神武大哭，曰：「自天柱薨背，賀六渾更何所仰！

translations.literal: Shenwu wept aloud and said, "Since the pillar Tianzhu passed, whom has Heliuhun to rely on!
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu wept and said, "Since the pillar Tianzhu died, whom has Heliuhun to lean on!

sentences.zh: 願大家千萬歲，以申力用。

translations.literal: I pray the great lord may live ten thousand years and lend his strength again.
translations.idiomatic: I pray you live ten thousand years and lend your strength again.

sentences.zh: 今旁人構間至此，大家何忍復出此言？

translations.literal: Now meddlers have set us at odds to this point; how can the great lord bear to speak so again?"
translations.idiomatic: Meddlers have set us at odds; how can you bear to speak so again?"

sentences.zh: 」兆投刀於地，遂刑白馬而盟，誓為兄弟，留宿夜飲。

translations.literal: Zhao cast the sword to the ground, slaughtered a white horse and swore alliance, vowed brotherhood, and stayed the night drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao threw down the sword, slew a white horse and swore alliance, vowed brotherhood, and stayed drinking through the night.

sentences.zh: 尉景伏壯士欲執兆，神武嚙臂止之，曰：「今殺之，其黨必奔歸聚結。

translations.literal: Jing had hidden strong men to seize Zhao; Shenwu bit his arm and stopped them, saying, "If we kill him now, his faction will surely flee and gather.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had hidden men to seize Zhao; Shenwu bit his arm and stopped them, saying, "Kill him now and his faction will scatter and regather.

sentences.zh: 兵饑馬瘦，不可相支。

translations.literal: With hungry troops and lean horses we cannot hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Hungry troops and lean horses cannot hold.

sentences.zh: 若英雄屈起，則為害滋甚。

translations.literal: If heroes rise in rebellion, the harm will be still greater.
translations.idiomatic: If heroes rise, the harm will be worse.

sentences.zh: 不如且置之。

translations.literal: It is better to let him go for now.
translations.idiomatic: Better to let him go for now.

sentences.zh: 兆雖勁捷，而凶狡無謀，不足圖也。

translations.literal: Zhao, though fierce and quick, was cruel and cunning without plan; he was not worth plotting against."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was fierce and quick but cruel and witless; he was not worth plotting against."

sentences.zh: 」旦日，兆歸營，又召神武。

translations.literal: The next day Zhao returned to camp and summoned Shenwu again.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Zhao returned to camp and summoned Shenwu again.

sentences.zh: 神武將上馬詣之，孫騰牽衣乃止。

translations.literal: Shenwu was about to mount and go to him; Sun Teng seized his garment and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu was about to ride to him; Sun Teng seized his robe and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 隔水肆罵，馳還晉陽。

translations.literal: He reviled Zhao across the water, then galloped back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed Zhao across the water and galloped back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 兆心腹念賢領降戶家累別為營。

translations.literal: Zhao's intimate Nian Xian led the surrendered households' families in a separate camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's man Nian Xian held the surrendered households' families in a separate camp.

sentences.zh: 神武偽與之善，觀其佩刀，因取之以殺其從者，盡散。

translations.literal: Shenwu pretended friendship, watched the blade at his belt, then took it and killed his attendants and dispersed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu feigned friendship, watched the blade at his belt, seized it, killed his attendants, and dispersed them.

sentences.zh: 於是士眾咸悅，倍願附從。

translations.literal: Thereupon soldiers and multitudes were all pleased and wished doubly to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers rejoiced and flocked to him in greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 初，魏真君中，內學者奏言上黨有天子氣，雲在壺關大王山。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenjun era of Wei, scholars of the inner learning memorialized that Shangdang had the aura of a Son of Heaven; the clouds were at King Mountain in Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei's Zhenjun era inner-court scholars reported Shangdang bore the aura of a Son of Heaven; clouds gathered at King Mountain in Huguan.

sentences.zh: 武帝於是南巡以厭當之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu therefore toured south to suppress it by facing it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu toured south to face it down.

sentences.zh: 累石為三封，斬其北鳳皇山以毀其形。

translations.literal: He piled stones into three mounds and cut down North Phoenix Mountain to destroy its form.
translations.idiomatic: He piled stones into three mounds and cut North Phoenix Mountain to break its form.

sentences.zh: 後上黨人居晉陽者號上黨坊，神武實居之。

translations.literal: Later men of Shangdang living in Jinyang called their quarter the Shangdang ward; Shenwu in fact lived there.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shangdang men in Jinyang called their quarter the Shangdang ward; Shenwu lived there.

sentences.zh: 及是行，舍大王山，六旬而進。

translations.literal: On this march he lodged at King Mountain and advanced after sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: On this march he lodged at King Mountain and advanced after sixty days.

sentences.zh: 將出滏口，倍加約束，纖毫之物，不聽侵犯。

translations.literal: As he was about to leave Fukou he redoubled discipline; not the slightest thing might be taken by force.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Fukou he tightened discipline; not the smallest thing might be taken.

sentences.zh: 將過麥地，神武輙步牽馬。

translations.literal: When he was about to pass through wheat fields, Shenwu always walked leading his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Passing wheat fields, Shenwu always walked and led his horse.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞之，皆稱高儀同將兵整肅，益歸心焉。

translations.literal: Near and far heard of it and all praised Director Gao for keeping his troops in order; hearts turned to him the more.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far praised Director Gao for strict troops; hearts turned to him the more.

sentences.zh: 遂前行屯鄴北，求糧於相州刺史劉誕，誕不供。

translations.literal: He advanced and camped north of Ye, asking grain of the Bing provincial inspector Liu Yan; Yan would not supply it.
translations.idiomatic: He camped north of Ye and asked grain of Inspector Liu Yan; Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 有軍營租米，神武自取之。

translations.literal: There was rent rice in the military camps; Shenwu took it himself.
translations.idiomatic: There was rent rice in the camps; Shenwu took it himself.

sentences.zh: 魏晉泰元年二月，神武軍次信都，高幹、封隆之開門以待，遂據冀州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jin and Wei and Tai, Shenwu's army halted at Xindu; Gao Gan and Feng Longzhi opened the gates to receive him, and he seized Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jin-Wei Tai year one Shenwu halted at Xindu; Gao Gan and Feng Longzhi opened the gates and he seized Ji.

sentences.zh: 是月，爾朱度律廢元曄而立節閔帝。

translations.literal: That month Erzhu Dulü deposed Ye and enthroned Emperor Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: That month Dulü deposed Ye and enthroned Emperor Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 欲羈縻神武，三月，乃白節閔帝，封神武為勃海王，征使入覲。

translations.literal: Wishing to bind Shenwu, in the third month they reported to Emperor Jiemin and enfeoffed Shenwu as Prince of Bohai and summoned him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to bind him, in the third month they reported to Jiemin, made Shenwu Prince of Bohai, and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 神武辭。

translations.literal: Shenwu declined.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu declined.

sentences.zh: 四月癸巳，又加授東道大行臺、第一鎮人酋長。

translations.literal: On the day guisi of the fourth month he was further appointed Grand Commander of the Eastern Circuit and chieftain of the first garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi of the fourth month he was further named Grand Commander of the Eastern Circuit and chieftain of the first garrison.

sentences.zh: 龐蒼鷹自太原來奔，神武以為行臺郎，尋以為安州刺史。

translations.literal: Pang Cangying came from Taiyuan to join him; Shenwu made him clerk of the Mobile Secretariat and soon made him Governor of An.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Cangying came from Taiyuan; Shenwu made him Mobile Secretariat clerk and soon governor of An.

sentences.zh: 神武自向山東，養士繕甲。

translations.literal: Shenwu himself turned toward Shandong, nurturing men and repairing armor.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu turned to Shandong, nurturing men and repairing armor.

sentences.zh: 禁兵侵掠，百姓歸心。

translations.literal: He forbade the army to plunder; the people gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade plunder; the people gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 乃詐為書，言爾朱兆將以六鎮人配契胡為部曲，眾皆愁。

translations.literal: He then forged a letter saying Erzhu Zhao would assign the men of the six garrisons as household troops to the Toba; the multitude was full of grief.
translations.idiomatic: He forged a letter saying Zhao would assign six-garrison men as Toba household troops; the host grieved.

sentences.zh: 又為并州符，征兵討步落稽。

translations.literal: He also forged a Bingzhou dispatch, calling up troops to campaign against the Buluoji.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged a Bingzhou dispatch calling up troops against the Buluoji.

sentences.zh: 發萬人將遣之，孫騰、尉景偽請留五日，如此者再。

translations.literal: Ten thousand men were mobilized to be sent; Sun Teng and Jing falsely asked to keep them five days; this was done twice.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand men were mobilized to march; Sun Teng and Jing falsely asked five days' delay; twice they did so.

sentences.zh: 神武親送之郊，雪涕執別。

translations.literal: Shenwu personally escorted them to the suburbs, weeping as he took leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu escorted them to the suburbs with tears as he took leave.

sentences.zh: 人號慟，哭聲動地。

translations.literal: Men wailed; the sound of crying shook the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Men wailed until the earth shook with crying.

sentences.zh: 神武乃喻之，曰：「與爾俱失鄉客，義同一家，不意在上乃爾徵召！

translations.literal: Shenwu then addressed them, saying, "I share with you the loss of our homeland; we are one family in righteousness; I never thought those above would summon you so!"
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu addressed them: "We share exile from home; we are one family; I never thought those above would summon you so!"

sentences.zh: 直向西已當死，後軍期又當死，配國人又當死，奈何？

translations.literal: Go west and you die at once; miss the rear deadline and you die again; be assigned to Toba households and you die again; what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: March west and you die; miss the deadline and you die; be assigned to Toba households and you die; what then?"

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「唯有反耳！

translations.literal: The multitude said, "There is nothing but to rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: The host cried, "Nothing but rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「反是急計，須推一人為主。

translations.literal: Shenwu said, "Rebellion is an urgent plan; we must push one man forward as leader."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "Rebellion is urgent; we must set one man above us."

sentences.zh: 」眾願奉神武。

translations.literal: The multitude wished to follow Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: The host wished to follow Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「爾鄉里難制，不見葛榮乎？

translations.literal: Shenwu said, "Your villages are hard to control; have you not seen Ge Rong?
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "Your villages are hard to rule; remember Ge Rong?

sentences.zh: 雖百萬眾，無刑法，終自灰滅。

translations.literal: Though he had a million followers, without law and punishment he was ashes in the end.
translations.idiomatic: A million men without law ended in ashes.

sentences.zh: 今以吾為主，當與前異。

translations.literal: Now if you take me as leader, it must differ from before.
translations.idiomatic: Take me as leader and it must differ from before.

sentences.zh: 不得欺漢兒，不得犯軍令，生死任吾，則可。

translations.literal: You must not cheat Han men, you must not break military law; life and death are mine to command; then it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Do not cheat Han men, do not break military law; life and death are mine; then we can proceed.

sentences.zh: 不爾，不能為取笑天下。

translations.literal: Otherwise I cannot make you a laughingstock for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I will not make the realm laugh at us.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆頓顙，死生唯命。

translations.literal: " All bowed their foreheads to the ground; life and death were his alone to command.
translations.idiomatic: " All bowed their foreheads; life and death were his to command.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「若不得已，明日，椎牛饗士，喻以討爾朱兆之意。」

translations.literal: Shenwu said, "If there is no other way, tomorrow we shall slaughter oxen and feast the troops, and explain the plan to campaign against Erzhu Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "If we must, tomorrow we slaughter oxen, feast the troops, and declare war on Erzhu Zhao."

sentences.zh: 封隆之進曰：「千載一時，普天幸甚。

translations.literal: Feng Longzhi advanced and said, "A moment once in a thousand years; all under Heaven is fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Longzhi stepped forward: "A moment that comes once in a thousand years; the realm is fortunate."

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「討賊，大順也。

translations.literal: " Shenwu said, "To punish rebels is the great accord.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenwu said, "To punish rebels is righteous.

sentences.zh: 拯時，大業也。

translations.literal: To rescue the age is the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: To rescue the age is great work.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不武，以死繼之，何敢讓焉。

translations.literal: Though I am not martial, I will follow with my death; how dare I yield?"
translations.idiomatic: I am not martial, but I will follow to the death; how dare I refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」六月庚子，建義於信都，尚未顯背爾朱氏。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi of the sixth month he raised righteousness at Xindu; he had not yet openly turned against the Erzhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi of the sixth month he raised the banner at Xindu, though he had not yet openly broken with the Erzhu.

sentences.zh: 及李元忠與高幹平殷州，斬爾朱羽生首來謁，神武撫膺曰：「今日反決矣！

translations.literal: When Li Yuanzhong and Gao Gan pacified Yin province and brought the head of Erzhu Yusheng to audience, Shenwu struck his breast and said, "Today the rebellion is settled!"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuanzhong and Gao Gan took Yin province and presented Erzhu Yusheng's head, Shenwu struck his breast and cried, "Today the break is final!"

sentences.zh: 」乃以元忠為殷州刺史。

translations.literal: " He then made Yuanzhong Governor of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Yuanzhong governor of Yin.

sentences.zh: 是時，兵威既振，乃抗表罪狀爾朱氏。

translations.literal: At that time, as military prestige was already rising, he submitted a memorial listing the Erzhu clan's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: His armies were strong now, and he sent up a memorial listing the Erzhu crimes.

sentences.zh: 世隆等秘表不通。

translations.literal: Shilong and the others suppressed the memorial and would not pass it through.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and others blocked the memorial.

sentences.zh: 八月，爾朱兆攻陷殷州，李元忠來奔。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Erzhu Zhao captured Yin province; Li Yuanzhong came to join Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhao took Yin province; Li Yuanzhong fled to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 孫騰以為朝廷隔絕，不權立天子，則眾望無所系。

translations.literal: Sun Teng held that with the court cut off, unless they provisionally enthroned a Son of Heaven, popular hope would have nothing to cling to.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng argued that with the court severed they must set up an emperor or the host would have nothing to follow.

sentences.zh: 十月壬寅，奉章武王融子勃海太守朗為皇帝，年號中興，是為廢帝。

translations.literal: On the day renyin of the tenth month they enthroned Lang, son of the Prince of Zhangwu Rong, Bohai commandery administrator, as emperor; the era name was Zhongxing; this is the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin of the tenth month they enthroned Lang, son of Prince Rong of Zhangwu, as emperor with era Zhongxing; this is the Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 時度律、仲遠軍次晉陽，爾朱兆會之。

translations.literal: At that time Dulü and Zhongyuan had their armies at Jinyang; Erzhu Zhao joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü and Zhongyuan camped at Jinyang; Zhao joined them.

sentences.zh: 神武用竇泰策，縱反間。

translations.literal: Shenwu used Dou Tai's stratagem and spread discord.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu used Dou Tai's plan and sowed discord.

sentences.zh: 度律、仲遠不戰而還，神武乃敗兆於廣阿。

translations.literal: Dulü and Zhongyuan withdrew without fighting; Shenwu then defeated Zhao at Guang'a.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü and Zhongyuan retreated without battle; Shenwu beat Zhao at Guang'a.

sentences.zh: 十一月，攻鄴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he attacked Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he attacked Ye.

sentences.zh: 相州刺史劉誕嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Bing provincial inspector Liu Yan held the city and defended it firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Liu Yan barred the gates and held firm.

sentences.zh: 神武起土山，為地道，往往建大柱，一時焚之，城陷入地。

translations.literal: Shenwu raised earthen hills and dug tunnels, often setting great posts that were burned at once; the wall collapsed into the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu raised earthworks and dug tunnels, set great posts and burned them at once; the wall sank into the ground.

sentences.zh: 麻祥時為湯陰令，神武呼之曰麻都，祥慚而逃。

translations.literal: Ma Xiang was then magistrate of Tangyin; Shenwu called him "Magistrate Ma"; Xiang fled in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiang was magistrate of Tangyin; Shenwu called him "Magistrate Ma"; Xiang fled in shame.

sentences.zh: 永熙元年正月壬午，拔鄴城，據之。

translations.literal: On the day renwu of the first month of the first year of Yongxi he took Ye city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu of the first month, Yongxi year one, he took Ye and held it.

sentences.zh: 廢帝進神武大丞相、柱國大將軍、太師。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor promoted Shenwu to Grand Chancellor, Pillar of State Grand General, and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor made Shenwu Grand Chancellor, Pillar of State Grand General, and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 是時，青州建義大都督崔靈珍、大都督耿翔皆遣使歸附，行汾州事劉貴棄城來降。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Lingzhen, Grand Commander of the righteous army of Qing province, and Geng Xiang, Grand Commander, both sent envoys to submit; Liu Gui, acting for Fen province, abandoned his city and came over.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lingzhen of Qing and Geng Xiang sent envoys to submit; Liu Gui abandoned Fen and came over.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，爾朱天光自長安，兆自并州，度律自洛陽，仲遠自東郡，同會鄴。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month Erzhu Tianguang came from Chang'an, Zhao from Bing province, Dulü from Luoyang, and Zhongyuan from Dong commandery; all converged on Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month Tianguang came from Chang'an, Zhao from Bing, Dulü from Luoyang, Zhongyuan from Dongjun; all converged on Ye.

sentences.zh: 眾號二十萬，挾洹水而軍。

translations.literal: They claimed two hundred thousand men and camped along the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed two hundred thousand and camped along the Huan.

sentences.zh: 節閔以長孫承業為大行臺，總督焉。

translations.literal: Jiemin appointed Changsun Chengye Grand Mobile Secretariat to command them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiemin named Changsun Chengye Grand Mobile Secretariat to command them.

sentences.zh: 神武令封隆之守鄴，自出頓紫陌。

translations.literal: Shenwu ordered Feng Longzhi to hold Ye and himself went out to camp at Zimo.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu left Feng Longzhi to hold Ye and camped at Zimo.

sentences.zh: 時馬不滿二千，步兵不至三萬，眾寡不敵。

translations.literal: At that time he had fewer than two thousand horses and not three thousand foot; the many could not match the few.
translations.idiomatic: He had fewer than two thousand horses and under three thousand foot; the odds were impossible.

sentences.zh: 乃於韓陵為圓陣，連牛驢以塞歸道。

translations.literal: He therefore formed a circular array at Hanling, linking oxen and donkeys to block the road of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling he formed a ring, chaining oxen and donkeys to cut off retreat.

sentences.zh: 於是將士皆為死誌，四面赴擊之。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers and soldiers all resolved to die; they struck from four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men resolved to die and struck from every side.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆責神武以背己。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao reproached Shenwu for betraying him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao reproached Shenwu for betrayal.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「本戮力者，共輔王室，今帝何在？

translations.literal: Shenwu said, "We joined forces to support the royal house together; where is the emperor now?
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "We joined to support the throne; where is the emperor now?

sentences.zh: 」兆曰：「永安枉害天柱，我報仇耳。

translations.literal: " Zhao said, "Yongan wrongly killed the pillar Tianzhu; I am only avenging him."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao said, "Yongan murdered the pillar Tianzhu; I seek revenge."

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「我昔日親聞天柱計，汝在戶前立，豈得言不反邪？

translations.literal: " Shenwu said, "I heard the pillar Tianzhu's plan with my own ears; you stood before the door; can you say you did not rebel?
translations.idiomatic: " Shenwu said, "I heard Tianzhu's plan myself; you stood at the door; will you deny you rebelled?

sentences.zh: 且以君殺臣，何報之有？

translations.literal: Moreover, when a lord kills his minister, what revenge is there?
translations.idiomatic: When a lord kills his minister, what revenge is owed?

sentences.zh: 今日義絕矣。

translations.literal: Today righteousness is at an end.
translations.idiomatic: Today our bond is dead.

sentences.zh: 」乃合戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: " They joined battle and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: " They fought and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆對慕容紹宗叩心曰：「不用公言，以此。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao beat his breast before Murong Shaozong and said, "Because I did not heed your words, this has come to pass."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao beat his breast before Shaozong: "Because I ignored you, this happened."

sentences.zh: 」將輕走，紹宗反旗鳴角，收聚散卒，成軍容而西上。

translations.literal: He was about to flee lightly; Shaozong turned the banners and sounded the horns, gathered the scattered troops, and re-formed an army bearing west.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to flee; Shaozong turned the banners, sounded horns, gathered the scattered, and marched west in order.

sentences.zh: 高季式以七騎追奔，度野馬崗，與兆遇。

translations.literal: Gao Jishi with seven horsemen pursued the fugitives, crossed Wild Horse Ridge, and met Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jishi with seven riders chased the rout, crossed Wild Horse Ridge, and met Zhao.

sentences.zh: 高昂望之不見，哭曰：「喪吾弟矣！

translations.literal: Gao Ang looked and could not see him; he wept and said, "I have lost my brother!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ang could not see him and wept, "I have lost my brother!"

sentences.zh: 」夜久，季式還，血滿袖。

translations.literal: After a long night Jishi returned, his sleeves drenched in blood.
translations.idiomatic: Deep into night Jishi returned, blood soaking his sleeves.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿倍道先據河橋。

translations.literal: Husi Chun by forced marches seized the River Bridge first.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun by forced marches seized the River Bridge.

sentences.zh: 初，普泰元年十月，歲星、熒惑、鎮星、太白聚於觜、參，色甚明。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the tenth month of the first year of Putai, Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Venus gathered at Zi and Shen, very bright.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai year one, tenth month, Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Venus gathered at Zi and Shen, blazing bright.

sentences.zh: 太史占雲，當有王者興。

translations.literal: The court astronomers divined that a king would rise.
translations.idiomatic: Court astronomers read that a king would rise.

sentences.zh: 是時，神武起於信都，至是而破兆等。

translations.literal: At that time Shenwu had risen at Xindu; by now he had broken Zhao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu had risen at Xindu; now he had broken Zhao.

sentences.zh: 四月，斛斯椿執天光、度律以送洛陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Husi Chun seized Tianguang and Dulü and sent them to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Husi Chun seized Tianguang and Dulü and sent them to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 長孫承業遣都督賈顯智、張歡入洛陽。

translations.literal: Changsun Chengye sent the commanders Jia Xianzhi and Zhang Huan into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Chengye sent Jia Xianzhi and Zhang Huan into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 執世隆、彥伯斬之。

translations.literal: They seized Shilong and Yanbo and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Shilong and Yanbo and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 兆奔并州。

translations.literal: Zhao fled to Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fled to Bing.

sentences.zh: 仲遠奔梁州，遂死焉。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan fled to Liang province and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan fled to Liang province and died there.

sentences.zh: 時凶蠹既除，朝廷慶悅。

translations.literal: When the vicious pests were removed, the court rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When the villains were gone, the court rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 初，未戰之前月，章武人張紹夜中忽被數騎將逾城至一大將軍前，敕紹為軍導向鄴。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the month before the battle, Zhang Shao of Zhangwu was suddenly taken by several horsemen over the wall before a great general, who ordered Shao to guide the army toward Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The month before battle, Zhang Shao of Zhangwu was seized by horsemen, carried over the wall before a great general, and ordered to guide the army to Ye.

sentences.zh: 雲佐受命者除殘賊。

translations.literal: He said the mandate-bearer would aid in destroying the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: He said heaven's chosen would aid in destroying the wicked.

sentences.zh: 紹回視之，兵不測，整疾無聲。

translations.literal: Shao looked back; the troops were beyond counting, marching in perfect silence.
translations.idiomatic: Shao looked back: troops beyond count, marching in perfect silence.

sentences.zh: 將至鄴，乃放焉。

translations.literal: When they were about to reach Ye they released him.
translations.idiomatic: Near Ye they released him.

sentences.zh: 及戰之日，爾朱氏軍人見陣外士馬四合，蓋神助也。

translations.literal: On the day of battle the Erzhu soldiers saw horsemen and foot closing in on four sides outside the array; it was divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: On battle day Erzhu soldiers saw hosts closing on four sides beyond the lines; heaven itself aided Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 既而神武至洛陽，廢節閔及中興主而立孝武。

translations.literal: Then Shenwu reached Luoyang, deposed Jiemin and the Zhongxing emperor, and enthroned Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu reached Luoyang, deposed Jiemin and the Zhongxing ruler, and set up Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 孝武既即位，授神武大丞相、天柱大將軍、太師，世襲定州刺史，增封並前十五萬戶。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu had taken the throne he appointed Shenwu Grand Chancellor, Pillar of Heaven Grand General, and Grand Preceptor, with hereditary governorship of Ding province and enfeoffment increased with the previous to one hundred fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu made Shenwu Grand Chancellor, Pillar of Heaven Grand General, Grand Preceptor, hereditary governor of Ding, and raised his fief to one hundred fifty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 神武辭天柱，減戶五萬。

translations.literal: Shenwu declined the Pillar of Heaven and reduced the households by fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu declined the Pillar of Heaven and cut fifty thousand households from his fief.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，還鄴，魏帝餞於幹脯山，執手而別。

translations.literal: On the day renchen he returned to Ye; the Wei emperor saw him off at Dried Meat Mountain and took his hand in parting.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he returned to Ye; the Wei emperor saw him off at Dried Meat Mountain and clasped his hand in farewell.

sentences.zh: 七月壬寅，神武帥師北伐爾朱兆。

translations.literal: On the day renyin of the seventh month Shenwu led troops north to campaign against Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin of the seventh month Shenwu marched north against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 封隆之言，侍中斛斯椿、賀拔勝、賈顯智等往事爾朱，普皆反噬。

translations.literal: Feng Longzhi said that Palace Attendants Husi Chun, Heba Sheng, Jia Xianzhi and others had formerly served the Erzhu and all turned to bite their masters.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Longzhi said Husi Chun, Heba Sheng, and Jia Xianzhi had served the Erzhu and now bit their masters.

sentences.zh: 今在京師寵任，必構禍隙。

translations.literal: Now favored at the capital, they would surely weave mischief.
translations.idiomatic: Favored at court now, they would surely breed trouble.

sentences.zh: 神武深以為然。

translations.literal: Shenwu deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu agreed completely.

sentences.zh: 乃歸天光、度律於京師，斬之。

translations.literal: He then sent Tianguang and Dulü back to the capital and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tianguang and Dulü to the capital and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 遂自滏口入。

translations.literal: He then entered through Fukou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered through Fukou.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆大掠晉陽，北保秀容，并州平。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao plundered Jinyang on a great scale, fled north to hold Xiurong, and Bing province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao plundered Jinyang, fled north to Xiurong, and Bing was pacified.

sentences.zh: 神武以晉陽四塞，乃建大丞相府而定居焉。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because Jinyang was closed on four sides, built the Grand Chancellor's mansion and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang was sealed on four sides; Shenwu built the Grand Chancellor's mansion and settled there.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆既至秀容，分兵守險，出入寇抄。

translations.literal: After Erzhu Zhao reached Xiurong he divided troops to hold the passes and went out raiding and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiurong Zhao split troops to hold passes and raided abroad.

sentences.zh: 神武揚聲討之，師出止者數四，兆意怠。

translations.literal: Shenwu proclaimed a campaign against him; the army set out and halted four times; Zhao grew slack.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu proclaimed war; his army marched and halted four times; Zhao grew careless.

sentences.zh: 神武揣其歲首當宴會，遣竇泰以精騎馳之。

translations.literal: Shenwu guessed that at the New Year he would hold a feast and sent Dou Tai with picked cavalry to rush him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu guessed a New Year feast and sent Dou Tai with elite horse to strike.

sentences.zh: 一日一夜行三百里，神武以大軍繼之。

translations.literal: In one day and one night they marched three hundred li; Shenwu followed with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In one day and night they rode three hundred li; Shenwu followed with the main host.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，竇泰奄至爾朱兆庭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Dou Tai suddenly reached Zhao's camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month, Dou Tai burst upon Zhao's camp.

sentences.zh: 軍人因宴休惰，忽見泰軍，驚走。

translations.literal: The army, feasting and resting in idleness, was startled and fled when they saw Tai's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting in idleness, the army fled at sight of Tai.

sentences.zh: 追破之於赤洪嶺。

translations.literal: They pursued and broke them at Red Flood Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued and broke them at Red Flood Ridge.

sentences.zh: 兆自縊。

translations.literal: Zhao hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 神武親臨，厚葬之。

translations.literal: Shenwu came in person and buried him with full honors.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu came in person and buried him with honor.

sentences.zh: 慕容紹宗以爾朱榮妻子及余眾自保烏突城。

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong with Erzhu Rong's wife and children and the remaining multitude held themselves in Wutu city.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong held Wutu with Rong's wife, children, and the remnant.

sentences.zh: 降，神武以義故待之甚厚。

translations.literal: They surrendered; Shenwu treated them very generously out of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: They surrendered; Shenwu treated them generously for old ties.

sentences.zh: 神武之入洛也，爾朱仲遠部下都督橋寧、張子期自滑臺歸命。

translations.literal: When Shenwu entered Luoyang, the commanders Qiao Ning and Zhang Ziqi under Erzhu Zhongyuan came from Huatai to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu entered Luoyang, Qiao Ning and Zhang Ziqi of Zhongyuan's command came from Huatai to submit.

sentences.zh: 神武以其助亂，且數反覆，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Shenwu because they had aided rebellion and had repeatedly turned coat, beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Because they had aided rebellion and turned coat repeatedly, Shenwu beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿由是內不自安，乃與南陽王寶炬及武衛將軍元毗、魏光祿、王思政構神武於魏帝。

translations.literal: Husi Chun was therefore ill at ease within and with the Prince of Nanyang Baoju and the Martial Guard General Yuan Pi, Wei Guanglu, and Wang Sizheng slandered Shenwu to the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun, uneasy within, joined Prince Baoju of Nanyang, Yuan Pi, Wei Guanglu, and Wang Sizheng to slander Shenwu to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 舍人元士弼又奏神武受敕大不敬，故魏帝心貳於賀拔嶽。

translations.literal: The Attendant Yuan Shibi also memorialized that Shenwu had been greatly disrespectful when receiving edicts; therefore the Wei emperor turned his heart toward Heba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Yuan Shibi memorialized Shenwu's disrespect toward edicts; the emperor turned his heart to Heba Yue.

sentences.zh: 初，孝明之時，洛下以兩拔相擊，謠言：「銅拔打鐵拔，元家世將末」。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the time of Xiaoming, in Luoyang two hairpins were struck together; a song said, "The bronze hairpin strikes the iron hairpin; the Yuan clan's generals are at an end."
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaoming's day Luoyang struck two hairpins together; a song ran, "Bronze hairpin strikes iron hairpin; the Yuan generals end."

sentences.zh: 好事者以二拔謂拓拔、賀拔，言俱將衰敗之兆。」

translations.literal: Those who delighted in such things took the two hairpins to mean Toba and Heba, saying both would decline and fall."
translations.idiomatic: Wits read the two hairpins as Toba and Heba, both doomed to fall."

sentences.zh: 時司空高幹密啟神武，言魏帝之貳。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Gao Gan secretly informed Shenwu of the Wei emperor's divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Gao Gan secretly told Shenwu the emperor was divided.

sentences.zh: 神武封呈，魏帝殺之。

translations.literal: Shenwu sealed it and presented it; the Wei emperor killed Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sealed the report and sent it up; the emperor killed Gan.

sentences.zh: 又遣東徐州刺史潘紹業密敕長樂太守龐蒼鷹，令殺其弟昂。

translations.literal: He also sent the Eastern Xuzhou inspector Pan Shaoye with a secret edict to the Changle administrator Pang Cangying to kill his brother Ang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pan Shaoye with a secret order to Pang Cangying to kill Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂先聞其兄死，以槊刺柱，伏壯士執紹業於路。

translations.literal: Ang had first heard of his brother's death; he drove his spear into a pillar, hid strong men, and seized Shaoye on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ang heard of his brother's death, drove his spear into a pillar, hid men, and seized Shaoye on the road.

sentences.zh: 得敕書於袍領，遂來奔。

translations.literal: He found the edict in the lining of the robe and came to join Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He found the edict in the robe lining and fled to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武抱其首哭曰：「天子枉害司空。

translations.literal: Shenwu embraced his head and wept, saying, "The Son of Heaven wrongly killed the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu held his head and wept: "The Son of Heaven wrongly killed the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 」遽使以白武幡勞其家屬。

translations.literal: " He immediately sent white martial banners to comfort his family.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent white martial banners at once to comfort the family.

sentences.zh: 時幹次弟慎在光州，為政嚴猛。

translations.literal: At that time Gan's next younger brother Shen was in Guang province; his government was severe and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Gan's brother Shen governed Guang province with severity.

sentences.zh: 又縱部下取納，魏帝使代之。

translations.literal: He also allowed his subordinates to take bribes; the Wei emperor sent someone to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: His men took bribes; the emperor sent a replacement.

sentences.zh: 慎聞難，將奔梁。

translations.literal: When Shen heard of the trouble he was about to flee to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the trouble, Shen prepared to flee to Liang.

sentences.zh: 其屬曰：「公家勛重，必不兄弟相反。

translations.literal: His followers said, "Your house's merit is great; brothers will surely not turn on each other."
translations.idiomatic: His men said, "Your house's merit is too great; brothers will not turn on each other."

sentences.zh: 」乃弊衣推鹿車歸勃海。

translations.literal: " He therefore wore rags and pushed a deer cart back to Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: " He wore rags, pushed a deer cart, and returned to Bohai.

sentences.zh: 逢使者，亦來奔。

translations.literal: He met the envoy on the road and came to join Shenwu as well.
translations.idiomatic: He met the envoy on the road and came to Shenwu as well.

sentences.zh: 於是魏帝與神武隙矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Wei emperor and Shenwu were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the Wei emperor and Shenwu were estranged.

sentences.zh: 阿至羅虜正光以前常稱籓，自魏朝多事，皆叛。

translations.literal: The Azhi-luo barbarians had called themselves vassals before Zhenguang; since the Wei court had many troubles, they all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Azhi-luo had been vassals before Zhenguang; when the Wei court fell into turmoil they all rebelled.

sentences.zh: 神武遣使招納，便附款。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent envoys to win them over and they submitted at once.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sent envoys and they submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔以寇賊平，罷行臺。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had abolished the Mobile Secretariat because bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with bandits pacified, an edict had abolished the Mobile Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至是以殊俗歸降，復授神武大行臺，隨機處分。

translations.literal: Now because foreign peoples submitted, Shenwu was again given the Grand Mobile Secretariat with discretionary power.
translations.idiomatic: Now foreign peoples submitted, and Shenwu was again given the Grand Mobile Secretariat with full discretion.

sentences.zh: 神武賫其粟帛，議者以為徒費無益。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent them grain and silk; critics thought it wasted effort without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sent grain and silk; critics called it waste.

sentences.zh: 神武不從。

translations.literal: Shenwu did not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu refused.

sentences.zh: 撫慰如初。

translations.literal: He comforted them as before.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted them as before.

sentences.zh: 其酋帥吐陳等感恩，皆從指麾。

translations.literal: Their chieftains such as Tuchen were grateful and all obeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains such as Tuchen were grateful and obeyed his command.

sentences.zh: 救曹泥，取万俟受洛幹，大收其用。

translations.literal: He rescued Cao Ni, took Wanqishou Luogan, and employed them to great effect.
translations.idiomatic: He rescued Cao Ni, took Wanqishou Luogan, and put both to great use.

sentences.zh: 河西費也頭虜紇豆陵伊利居苦池河，恃險擁眾。

translations.literal: The Feiyetou barbarian Hedouling Yili lived on the Ku River in Hexi, trusting the terrain and hoarding a multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yili of the Feiyetou He held the Ku River in Hexi, trusting the terrain and hoarding followers.

sentences.zh: 神武遣長史侯景屢招不從。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent Chief Clerk Hou Jing to summon him repeatedly; he would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sent Hou Jing to summon him again and again; he refused.

sentences.zh: 天平元年正月壬辰，神武西伐費也頭虜紇豆陵伊利於河西，滅之。

translations.literal: On the day renchen of the first month of the first year of Tianping, Shenwu campaigned west against Yili of the Feiyetou in Hexi and destroyed him.
