translations.idiomatic: On renchen of the first month, Tianping year one, Shenwu campaigned west against Yili in Hexi and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 遷其部落於河東。

translations.literal: He moved their tribes to the east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He moved their tribes east of the river.

sentences.zh: 二月，永寧寺九層浮屠災。

translations.literal: In the second month the nine-story pagoda of Yongning Temple burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the nine-story pagoda of Yongning Temple burned.

sentences.zh: 既而人有從東萊至。

translations.literal: Then someone came from Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Then someone arrived from Donglai.

sentences.zh: 雲及海上人咸見之於海中，俄而霧起，乃滅。

translations.literal: Clouds and people on the sea all saw it in the ocean; soon mist rose and it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds and seafarers saw it on the ocean; mist rose and it vanished.

sentences.zh: 說者以為天意。

translations.literal: Those who spoke of it took it for heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Observers called it heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 若曰：「永寧見災，魏不寧矣。

translations.literal: As if to say, "When Yongning meets disaster, Wei will not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: As if to say, "Yongning burns and Wei will not rest.

sentences.zh: 飛入東海，勃海應矣。

translations.literal: It flies into the Eastern Sea; Bohai answers."
translations.idiomatic: It flies to the Eastern Sea; Bohai answers."

sentences.zh: 」魏帝既有異圖，時侍中封隆之與孫騰私言。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor already harbored other designs; at that time Palace Attendant Feng Longzhi spoke privately with Sun Teng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already plotted; Feng Longzhi spoke privately with Sun Teng.

sentences.zh: 隆之喪妻，魏帝欲妻以從妹。

translations.literal: Longzhi had lost his wife; the Wei emperor wished to marry him to a cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi's wife had died; the emperor wished to give him a cousin in marriage.

sentences.zh: 騰亦未之信。

translations.literal: Teng also did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Teng did not believe it either.

sentences.zh: 心害隆之，泄其言於斛斯椿。

translations.literal: He resented Longzhi in his heart and leaked his words to Husi Chun.
translations.idiomatic: He resented Longzhi and leaked his words to Husi Chun.

sentences.zh: 椿以白魏帝。

translations.literal: Chun reported it to the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chun told the emperor.

sentences.zh: 又孫騰帶仗入省，擅殺御史。

translations.literal: Also Sun Teng entered the palace armed and killed a censor on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng entered the palace armed and killed a censor.

sentences.zh: 並亡來奔。

translations.literal: Both fled and came to join Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Both fled to Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 稱魏帝撾舍人梁續於前。

translations.literal: They said the Wei emperor had beaten the attendant Liang Xu before the court.
translations.idiomatic: They said the emperor had beaten attendant Liang Xu before the court.

sentences.zh: 光祿少卿元子幹攘臂擊之，謂騰曰：「語爾高王，元家兒拳正如此。

translations.literal: Guanglu Junior Minister Yuan Zigan rolled up his sleeves and struck him, saying to Teng, "Tell your Duke of Gao: the Yuan boy's fist is just like this."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zigan struck him and told Teng, "Tell the Duke of Gao: a Yuan fist is just like this."

sentences.zh: 」領軍婁昭辭疾歸晉陽。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Lou Zhao pleaded illness and returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao pleaded illness and returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 魏帝於是以斛斯椿兼領軍，分置督將及河南、關西諸刺史。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor then made Husi Chun acting Commander-in-Chief and posted supervising generals and governors of Henan and Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Husi Chun acting commander and posted supervisors across Henan and Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 華山王鷙在徐州，神武使邸珍奪其管龠。

translations.literal: Prince Zhi of Huashan was at Xuzhou; Shenwu sent Di Zhen to seize his seals and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhi of Huashan held Xuzhou; Shenwu sent Di Zhen to seize his seals.

sentences.zh: 建州刺史韓賢、濟州刺史蔡俊皆神武同義，魏帝忌之。

translations.literal: Jian provincial inspector Han Xian and Ji provincial inspector Cai Jun had both risen with Shenwu; the Wei emperor resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian of Jian and Cai Jun of Ji had risen with Shenwu; the emperor resented them.

sentences.zh: 故省建州以去賢，使御史中尉綦俊察俊罪，以開府賈顯智為濟州，俊拒之。

translations.literal: Therefore he abolished Jian province to remove Xian, sent the Censorate Director Qi Jun to investigate Jun's crimes, and named Jia Xianzhi as Governor of Ji; Jun refused.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished Jian to remove Xian, sent Qi Jun against Cai Jun, and named Jia Xianzhi governor of Ji; Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 魏帝逾怒。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 五月，下詔，雲將征句吳，發河南諸州兵，增宿衛，守河橋。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he issued an edict saying he would campaign against Wu and mobilized troops of the Henan provinces, increased the palace guard, and held the River Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he announced a campaign against Wu, mobilized Henan, increased the guard, and held the River Bridge.

sentences.zh: 六月丁巳，密詔神武曰：「宇文黑獺自平破秦、隴，多求非分，脫有變非常，事資經略。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi of the sixth month he secretly edicted Shenwu, "Yuwen Heituo, since pacifying Qin and Long, demands much beyond measure; if he turns rebel unexpectedly, the matter requires planning.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi of the sixth month he secretly wrote Shenwu that Yuwen Heituo demanded too much since Qin and Long fell, and any rebellion would need planning.

sentences.zh: 但表啟未全背戾，進討事涉匆匆。

translations.literal: Yet his memorials do not yet show full defiance; to advance would be hasty.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were not yet openly rebellious; to strike would be rash.

sentences.zh: 遂召群臣，議其可否。

translations.literal: I have therefore summoned the ministers to debate whether we should.
translations.idiomatic: I have summoned ministers to debate.

sentences.zh: 僉言假稱南伐，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: All said to feign a southern campaign and alert within and without.
translations.idiomatic: All said to feign war in the south and alert the realm.

sentences.zh: 一則防黑獺不虞，二則可威吳楚。

translations.literal: One, to guard against Heituo's surprise; two, to overawe Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: One, to guard against Heituo; two, to overawe Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 」時魏帝將伐神武。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei emperor was about to campaign against Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to march against Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 神武部署將帥，慮疑，故有此詔。

translations.literal: Shenwu deployed his generals; fearing suspicion, he therefore had this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu deployed generals; fearing suspicion, he used this edict.

sentences.zh: 神武乃表曰：「荊州綰接蠻左，密邇畿服。

translations.literal: Shenwu then memorialized, "Jing province borders the barbarians of the left and lies close to the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu memorialized: "Jing borders barbarians and lies near the capital.

sentences.zh: 關隴恃遠，將有逆圖。

translations.literal: Guan and Long rely on distance and will plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Long rely on distance and will rebel.

sentences.zh: 臣今潛勒兵馬三萬，擬從河東而渡。

translations.literal: Your servant now secretly leads thirty thousand horse, planning to cross from the east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead thirty thousand horse to cross east of the river.

sentences.zh: 又遣恒州刺史庫狄幹，瀛州刺史郭瓊，汾州刺史斛律金，前武衛大將軍彭樂擬兵四萬，從其來違津渡。

translations.literal: Also sent Hengzhou inspector Kudili Gan, Yingzhou inspector Guo Qiong, Fenzhou inspector Hulu Jin, and former Martial Guard Grand General Peng Yue with forty thousand to meet any crossing at the ford.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Kudili Gan, Guo Qiong, Hulu Jin, and Peng Yue with forty thousand to hold the ford.

sentences.zh: 遣領軍將軍婁昭，相州刺史竇泰，前瀛州刺史堯雄，并州刺史高隆之擬兵五萬，以討荊州。

translations.literal: Sent Commander Lou Zhao, Xiangzhou inspector Dou Tai, former Yingzhou inspector Yao Xiong, and Bingzhou inspector Gao Longci with fifty thousand to strike Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lou Zhao, Dou Tai, Yao Xiong, and Gao Longci with fifty thousand against Jing.

sentences.zh: 遣冀州刺史尉景，前冀州刺史高敖曹，濟州刺史蔡俊，前侍中封隆之，擬山東兵七萬，突騎五萬，以征江左。

translations.literal: Sent Ji inspector Jing, former Ji inspector Gao Aocao, Ji inspector Cai Jun, and former Palace Attendant Feng Longzhi with seventy thousand eastern troops and fifty thousand raiders to campaign on the Jiang left.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jing, Gao Aocao, Cai Jun, and Feng Longzhi with seventy thousand foot and fifty thousand raiders against the Jiang left.

sentences.zh: 皆約勒所部，伏聽處分。

translations.literal: All were ordered to restrain their commands and await disposition.
translations.idiomatic: All were ordered to await his command.

sentences.zh: 」魏帝知覺其變，乃出神武表，命群官議之，欲止神武諸軍。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor, knowing he had detected the change, produced Shenwu's memorial and ordered the officials to debate, wishing to halt Shenwu's armies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor produced the memorial and ordered debate, wishing to halt the armies.

sentences.zh: 神武乃集在並僚佐，令其博議。

translations.literal: Shenwu then gathered his staff at Bing and ordered broad debate.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu gathered his Bing staff and ordered debate.

sentences.zh: 還以表聞，仍以信誓自明忠款曰：「臣為嬖佞所間，陛下一旦賜疑，令猖狂之罪，爾朱時計。

translations.literal: He sent the memorial again and with oath declared his loyalty, saying, "Your servant was set at odds by favored minions; Your Majesty suddenly gave suspicion, and the charge of recklessness is the Erzhu plan repeated.
translations.idiomatic: He swore loyalty: "Favored minions set us at odds; Your Majesty suddenly doubted me; this charge of recklessness repeats the Erzhu day.

sentences.zh: 臣若不盡誠竭節，敢負陛下，則使身受天殃，子孫殄絕。

translations.literal: If your servant does not exhaust loyalty to the utmost, daring to fail Your Majesty, may my body suffer heaven's calamity and my sons and grandsons be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: If I fail in loyalty, may heaven punish me and my line end.

sentences.zh: 陛下若垂信赤心，使干戈不動，佞臣一二人，願斟量廢出。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will trust this loyal heart and let weapons rest, one or two slanderers, I beg you weigh removing them."
translations.idiomatic: If you trust me and let weapons rest, remove one or two slanderers."

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝復錄在京文武議意，以答神武。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei the emperor again recorded the views of civil and military officials at the capital and replied to Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the emperor recorded capital opinion and replied.

sentences.zh: 使舍人溫子升草敕，子升逡巡未敢作。

translations.literal: He had Attendant Wen Zisheng draft the edict; Zisheng hesitated and dared not write.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wen Zisheng to draft the edict; Zisheng hesitated.

sentences.zh: 帝據胡床拔劍作色，子升乃為敕曰：前持心血，遠以示王，深冀彼此共相禮悉。

translations.literal: The emperor sat on a folding chair, drew his sword, and showed anger; Zisheng then wrote the edict saying: Earlier I sent my heart's blood far to show the king, deeply hoping we would understand each other.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew his sword in anger; Zisheng then wrote: I sent my heart to you hoping for mutual trust.

sentences.zh: 而不良之徒，坐生間貳。

translations.literal: Yet wicked men sitting idle bred division.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men bred division.

sentences.zh: 近孫騰倉卒向彼，致使聞者疑有異謀。

translations.literal: Recently Sun Teng went to you in haste, making hearers suspect strange designs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng's hasty visit made hearers suspect treason.

sentences.zh: 故遣御史中尉綦俊，具申朕懷。

translations.literal: Therefore I sent Censorate Director Qi Jun to state my heart fully.
translations.idiomatic: I sent Qi Jun to state my heart.

sentences.zh: 今得王啟，言誓懇惻。

translations.literal: Now receiving the king's memorial, the oath is earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Your memorial's oath is earnest.

sentences.zh: 反覆思之，猶所未解。

translations.literal: Turning it over in mind, I still do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Turning it over, I still do not understand.

sentences.zh: 以朕眇身，遇王武略，不勞尺刃，坐為天子。

translations.literal: With my slight person, meeting the king's martial strategy, without laboring a foot of blade I sat as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: By your strategy I became Son of Heaven without drawing a blade.

sentences.zh: 所謂生我者父母，貴我者高王。

translations.literal: They say those who give me life are my parents; those who ennoble me are the Duke of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: They say my parents gave me life; the Duke of Gao ennobled me.

sentences.zh: 今若無事背王，規相攻討，則使身及子孫。

translations.literal: If now without cause I turn against the king and plot attack, may it be as the oath says for body and sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: If I turn against you without cause, may the oath fall on me and my sons.

sentences.zh: 還如王誓。

translations.literal: As the king swore.
translations.idiomatic: As you swore.

sentences.zh: 皇天后土，實聞此言。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth truly hear these words.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth hear.

sentences.zh: 近慮宇文為亂，賀拔勝應之。

translations.literal: Recently I feared Yuwen's disorder and Heba Sheng's response.
translations.idiomatic: I feared Yuwen's disorder and Heba Sheng's answer.

sentences.zh: 故纂嚴，欲與王俱為聲援。

translations.literal: Therefore I gathered troops, wishing to support the king as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I gathered troops to support you.

sentences.zh: 宇文今日使者相望，觀其所為，更無異跡。

translations.literal: Yuwen's envoys come and go today; watching his conduct, there is no other sign.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen's envoys come and go; I see no other sign.

sentences.zh: 賀拔在南，開拓邊境，為國立功，念無可責。

translations.literal: Heba in the south opens the frontier and serves the state; considering his merit, he cannot be blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Heba in the south serves the state; he cannot be blamed.

sentences.zh: 君若欲分討，何以為辭？

translations.literal: If you wish to divide and strike, with what words will you go?
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to strike separately, what excuse have you?

sentences.zh: 東南不賓，為日己久。

translations.literal: The southeast has not submitted for a long day.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast has long refused submission.

sentences.zh: 先朝已來，置之度外，今天下戶口減半，未宜窮兵極武。

translations.literal: Former courts put it outside concern; now the realm's households are halved; we should not exhaust arms to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Former courts ignored it; households are halved; we must not exhaust arms.

sentences.zh: 朕既暗昧，不知佞人是誰。

translations.literal: I am myself dim; I do not know who the slanderers are.
translations.idiomatic: I am dim; I do not know the slanderers.

sentences.zh: 可列其姓名，令朕知也。

translations.literal: List their names so I may know.
translations.idiomatic: Name them so I may know.

sentences.zh: 如聞庫狄幹語王云：「本欲取懦弱者為主，無事立此長君，使其不可駕御。

translations.literal: I hear Kudili Gan told the king, "We meant to take a weakling as lord; for nothing we set up this tall lord, making him impossible to control.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Kudili Gan told you, "We meant a weakling; instead we set up this tall lord impossible to control.

sentences.zh: 今但作十五日行，自可廢之，更立余者。

translations.literal: Make a fifteen-day march now and we can depose him and set up another."
translations.idiomatic: March fifteen days and we can depose him and set up another."

sentences.zh: 」如此議論，自是王間勛人，豈出佞臣之口？

translations.literal: Such talk is surely from the king's own meritorious men; how could it come from slanderers' mouths?
translations.idiomatic: Such talk comes from your own men, not from slanderers.

sentences.zh: 去歲封隆之背叛，今年孫騰逃走，不罪不送，誰不怪王？

translations.literal: Last year Feng Longzhi rebelled; this year Sun Teng fled; neither punished nor sent back; who does not marvel at the king?
translations.idiomatic: Feng Longzhi rebelled last year; Sun Teng fled this year; neither punished; who does not wonder?

sentences.zh: 騰既為禍始，曾無愧懼。

translations.literal: Teng was the source of disaster yet felt no shame or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Teng began the disaster yet felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 王若事君盡誠，何不斬送二首？

translations.literal: If the king serves the lord with full loyalty, why not behead and send the two heads?
translations.idiomatic: If you are loyal, why not send their heads?

sentences.zh: 王雖啟圖西去，而四道俱進。

translations.literal: Though the king declares intent to go west, four routes advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Though you declare the west, four routes advance.

sentences.zh: 或欲南度洛陽，或欲東臨江左。

translations.literal: Some wish to cross south to Luoyang; some wish to press east to the Jiang left.
translations.idiomatic: Some aim at Luoyang; some at the Jiang left.

sentences.zh: 言之者猶應自怪，聞之者寧能不疑？

translations.literal: Those who speak of it should themselves find it strange; those who hear, how can they not doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Speakers should find it strange; hearers must doubt.

sentences.zh: 王若守誠不貳，晏然居北，在此雖有百萬之眾，終無圖彼之心。

translations.literal: If the king keeps faith without duplicity and rests calmly in the north, though I have a million here I will never plot against you.
translations.idiomatic: If you keep faith in the north, though I have a million I will never plot against you.

sentences.zh: 王脫信邪棄義，舉旗南指，縱無匹馬只輪，猶欲奮空拳而爭死。

translations.literal: If the king trusts evil and abandons righteousness and raises banners south, though not a horse or wheel remains I will still fight with empty fists to the death.
translations.idiomatic: If you abandon righteousness and march south, I will fight with empty fists.

sentences.zh: 朕本寡德，王已立之，百姓無知，或謂實可。

translations.literal: I am by nature lacking in virtue; the king already established me; the people, not knowing, may think it possible.
translations.idiomatic: I lack virtue; you established me; the people may think it possible.

sentences.zh: 若為他所圖，則彰朕之惡。

translations.literal: If another plots against me, it will show my wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: If another plots me, it shows my wickedness.

sentences.zh: 假令還為王殺，幽辱齏粉，了無遺恨。

translations.literal: Even if I am killed for the king, humiliated and ground to powder, I will have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you kill me, ground to powder, I will not regret.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 王既以德見推，以義見舉，一朝背德舍義，便是過有所歸。

translations.literal: The king was promoted for virtue and raised for righteousness; to turn against virtue and abandon righteousness in one morning is to have a place for fault.
translations.idiomatic: You were raised for virtue and righteousness; to abandon both in one morning is fault.

sentences.zh: 本望君臣一體，若合符契，不圖今日，分疏到此！

translations.literal: I originally hoped ruler and minister would be one body, fitting like tally halves; I never thought today we would be estranged to this point!
translations.idiomatic: I hoped ruler and minister would be one; I never thought we would come to this!

sentences.zh: 古語云：「越人射我，笑而道之；

translations.literal: The old saying runs, "When a Yue man shoots me, I laugh and speak of it;
translations.idiomatic: The old saying says, "When a Yue man shoots me, I laugh;

sentences.zh: 吾兄射我，泣而道之。

translations.literal: when my elder brother shoots me, I weep and speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: when my brother shoots me, I weep."

sentences.zh: 」朕既親王，情如兄弟，所以投筆拊膺，不覺歔欷。

translations.literal: I am close kin to the king; our feeling is like brothers; therefore I throw down the brush and beat my breast, unable to restrain sobs.
translations.idiomatic: You are my kin as to a brother; I throw down the brush and sob.

sentences.zh: 初，神武自京師將北，以為洛陽久經喪亂，王氣衰盡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shenwu was about to go north from the capital, he thought Luoyang had long suffered disorder and royal aura was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu was about to leave the capital for the north, he thought Luoyang's royal aura was spent.

sentences.zh: 雖有山河之固，土地褊狹，不如鄴，請遷都。

translations.literal: Though it had the security of mountains and rivers, the land was narrow; it was not as good as Ye; he asked to move the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Though defended by mountains and rivers, the land was narrow; Ye was better; he asked to move the capital.

sentences.zh: 魏帝曰：「高祖定鼎河洛，為永永之基。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor said, "Gaozu fixed the tripod at He and Luo as a foundation forever."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Gaozu fixed the tripod at He and Luo forever."

sentences.zh: 經營制度，至世宗乃畢。

translations.literal: Institutions were managed and the system completed only under Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions were completed only under Shizong.

sentences.zh: 王既功在社稷，宜遵太和舊事。

translations.literal: The king's merit is to the altars of state; he should follow the old affairs of Taihe."
translations.idiomatic: Your merit is to the state; follow Taihe precedent."

sentences.zh: 」神武奉詔。

translations.literal: Shenwu received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu obeyed.

sentences.zh: 至是，復謀焉。

translations.literal: At this he again plotted.
translations.idiomatic: Now he plotted again.

sentences.zh: 遣兵千騎鎮建興，益河東及濟州兵，於白溝虜船，不聽向洛，諸州和糴粟，運入鄴城。

translations.literal: He sent a thousand horse to garrison Jianxing, increased troops of Hedong and Ji, seized boats on the White Ditch and forbade passage to Luo, had the provinces contribute grain, and transported it into Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Jianxing, increased eastern troops, seized White Ditch boats, barred the road to Luo, and shipped grain to Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏帝又敕神武曰：「王若厭伏人情，杜絕物議，唯有歸河東之兵，罷建興之戍，送相州之粟，追濟州之軍，令蔡俊受代，使邸珍出徐。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor again edicted Shenwu, "If the king wishes to calm popular feeling and stop talk, return the troops east of the river, disband the Jianxing garrison, send Xiangzhou grain, recall Ji troops, have Cai Jun replaced, and send Di Zhen out of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote: return eastern troops, disband Jianxing, send grain, recall Ji, replace Cai Jun, remove Di Zhen from Xu.

sentences.zh: 止戈散馬，各事家業。

translations.literal: Stop weapons and scatter horses; each attend to his household.
translations.idiomatic: Lay down arms; each return home.

sentences.zh: 脫須糧廩，別遣轉輸。

translations.literal: If grain is needed, send transport separately.
translations.idiomatic: If grain is needed, send it separately.

sentences.zh: 則讒人結舌，疑悔不生。

translations.literal: Then slanderers will hold their tongues and doubt will not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Then slanderers will fall silent.

sentences.zh: 王高枕太原，朕垂拱京洛，終不舉足渡河，以干戈相指。

translations.literal: The king may rest high pillow at Taiyuan; I will rule from the capital with folded arms; I will never cross the river with arms.
translations.idiomatic: Rest at Taiyuan; I rule from the capital; I will never cross the river in arms.

sentences.zh: 王若馬首南向，問鼎輕重，朕雖無武，欲止不能。

translations.literal: If the king turns his horse south and asks the weight of the tripod, though I lack martial virtue I cannot stop myself.
translations.idiomatic: If you turn south and seize the realm, I cannot stop myself.

sentences.zh: 必為社稷宗廟，出萬死之策。

translations.literal: I must for the altars of state and the ancestral temple devise a plan of ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: For state and temple I must risk death.

sentences.zh: 決在於王，非朕能定。

translations.literal: The decision lies with the king; it is not within my power to settle.
translations.idiomatic: The decision is yours, not mine.

sentences.zh: 為山止簣，相為惜之。」

translations.literal: To stop building a mountain one basket short is to pity each other."
translations.idiomatic: To stop one basket short is mutual pity."

sentences.zh: 魏帝時以任祥為兼尚書左僕射，加開府。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei emperor made Ren Xiang acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat with Grand Opening.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Ren Xiang acting Left Vice Director with Grand Opening.

sentences.zh: 祥棄官走至河北，據郡待神武。

translations.literal: Xiang abandoned office and fled to Hebei, holding a commandery awaiting Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang fled to Hebei and held a commandery for Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 魏帝乃敕文武官，北來者任去留。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor then ordered civil and military officials that those coming from the north might stay or leave as they chose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor allowed northern officials to stay or leave.

sentences.zh: 下詔罪狀神武，為北伐經營。

translations.literal: He issued an edict listing Shenwu's crimes and campaigned north.
translations.idiomatic: He listed Shenwu's crimes and marched north.

sentences.zh: 神武亦勒馬宣告曰：「孤遇爾朱擅權，舉大義於四海。

translations.literal: Shenwu also reined his horse and proclaimed, "I met the Erzhu seizing power and raised great righteousness throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu proclaimed: I met Erzhu tyranny and raised righteousness across the seas.

sentences.zh: 奉戴主上，義貫幽明。

translations.literal: I supported the sovereign above; righteousness pierced dark and light.
translations.idiomatic: I supported the sovereign; my righteousness was clear.

sentences.zh: 橫為斛斯椿讒構，以誠節為逆首。

translations.literal: I was wrongly framed by Husi Chun; sincerity was made rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun framed me; sincerity was called treason.

sentences.zh: 昔趙鞅興晉陽之甲，誅君側惡人。

translations.literal: In old days Zhao Yang raised the army of Jinyang to punish evil men at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yang raised Jinyang to punish evil at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 今者南邁，誅椿而已。

translations.literal: Today marching south is only to execute Chun."
translations.idiomatic: Today I march south only to kill Chun."

sentences.zh: 」以高昂為前鋒，曰：「若用司空言，豈有今日之舉！

translations.literal: He made Gao Ang vanguard, saying, "If we had used the Minister of Works' counsel, how could we have today's move!"
translations.idiomatic: He made Gao Ang vanguard: "Had we listened to the Minister of Works, we would not march today!"

sentences.zh: 」司馬子如答神武曰：「本欲立小者，正為此耳。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru answered Shenwu, "We meant to set up a lesser man precisely for this."
translations.idiomatic: Ziru said, "We meant a lesser man for this very reason."

sentences.zh: 」魏帝征兵關右。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor mobilized troops west of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mobilized western troops.

sentences.zh: 召賀拔勝赴行在所，遣大行臺長孫承業、大都督潁川王斌之、斛斯椿共鎮武牢。

translations.literal: He summoned Heba Sheng to the imperial camp and sent Grand Mobile Secretariat Changsun Chengye, Grand Commander Prince Binzhi of Yingchuan, and Husi Chun to hold Wulao together.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Heba Sheng and sent Chengye, Prince Binzhi, and Chun to hold Wulao.

sentences.zh: 汝陽王暹鎮石濟，行臺長孫子彥帥前恒農太守元洪略鎮陜，賈顯智率豫州刺史斛斯元壽伐蔡俊。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Ruyang held Shiji; Mobile Secretariat Chief Sun Ziyan with former Hengnong administrator Yuan Honglue held Shaan; Jia Xianzhi led Yuzhou inspector Husi Yuanshou against Cai Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian held Shiji; Sun Ziyan and Yuan Honglue held Shaan; Jia Xianzhi and Husi Yuanshou struck Cai Jun.

sentences.zh: 神武使竇泰與左箱大都督莫多婁貸文逆顯智，韓賢逆暹。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent Dou Tai and Left Wing Grand Commander Moduolou Daiwen against Xianzhi; Han Xian against Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sent Dou Tai and Daiwen against Xianzhi; Han Xian against Xian.

sentences.zh: 元壽軍降泰。

translations.literal: Yuanshou's army surrendered to Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshou surrendered to Tai.

sentences.zh: 貸文與顯智遇於長壽津，顯智陰約降，引軍退。

translations.literal: Daiwen met Xianzhi at Longevity Ford; Xianzhi secretly agreed to surrender and withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: At Longevity Ford Xianzhi secretly agreed to surrender and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 軍司元玄覺之，馳還請益師。

translations.literal: Army clerk Yuan Xuan noticed and galloped back to ask for more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xuan noticed and galloped for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 魏帝遣大都督侯幾紹赴之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent Grand Commander Hou Jishao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Hou Jishao.

sentences.zh: 戰於滑臺東。

translations.literal: They fought east of Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: They fought east of Huatai.

sentences.zh: 顯智以軍降，紹死之。

translations.literal: Xianzhi surrendered with his army; Shao died.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi surrendered; Shao died.

sentences.zh: 七月，魏帝躬率大眾屯河橋。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Wei emperor personally led the great host and camped at the River Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor camped at the River Bridge.

sentences.zh: 神武至河北十餘里，再遣口申誠款，魏帝不報。

translations.literal: Shenwu came within ten-odd li of Hebei and twice sent oral messages of loyalty; the Wei emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten li of Hebei Shenwu sent loyalty twice; the emperor did not answer.

sentences.zh: 神武乃引軍度河。

translations.literal: Shenwu then led his army across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 魏帝問計於群臣。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor asked counsel of his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers.

sentences.zh: 或雲南依賀拔勝，或云西就關中，或云守洛口死戰，未決。

translations.literal: Some said to rely south on Heba Sheng, some to go west to Guanzhong, some to die fighting at Luokou; no decision was made.
translations.idiomatic: Some said rely on Heba Sheng, some go to Guanzhong, some die at Luokou; none decided.

sentences.zh: 而元斌之與斛斯椿爭權不睦，斌之棄椿徑還，紿帝雲神武兵至。

translations.literal: Yuan Binzhi and Husi Chun contended for power without harmony; Binzhi abandoned Chun and returned straightway, deceiving the emperor that Shenwu's troops had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Binzhi quarreled with Chun, fled back, and lied that Shenwu had arrived.

sentences.zh: 即日，魏帝遜於長安。

translations.literal: That very day the Wei emperor withdrew to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 己酉，神武入洛，停於永寧寺。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou Shenwu entered Luo and stopped at Yongning Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Shenwu entered Luo and stopped at Yongning Temple.

sentences.zh: 八月甲寅，召集百官謂曰：「為臣奉主，匡救危亂。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin of the eighth month he summoned the hundred officials and said, "As ministers serving the lord, we rescue danger and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he summoned officials: ministers must rescue danger.

sentences.zh: 若處不諫爭，出不陪隨，緩則耽寵爭榮，急便竄失，臣節安在！」

translations.literal: If at court one does not remonstrate, and on campaign one does not follow, in ease one clings to favor and fights for glory, in urgency one flees and is lost, where is the minister's integrity!"
translations.idiomatic: Without remonstrance at court and company on campaign, where is integrity?"

sentences.zh: 遂收開府儀同三司叱列延慶、兼尚書左僕射辛雄、兼吏部尚書崔孝芬、都官尚書劉廞、兼度支尚書楊機、散騎常侍元士弼，並殺之，誅其貳也。

translations.literal: He then seized Grand Opening Chilie Yanqing, acting Left Vice Director Xin Xiong, acting Personnel Director Cui Xiaofen, Justice Director Liu Yin, acting Revenue Director Yang Ji, and Regular Attendant Yuan Shibi, and killed them all to punish disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yanqing, Xin Xiong, Cui Xiaofen, Liu Yin, Yang Ji, and Yuan Shibi and killed them for disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 士弼籍沒家口。

translations.literal: Shibi's household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi's household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 神武以萬機不可曠廢，乃與百僚議。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because the myriad affairs could not be left idle, deliberated with the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu deliberated with officials because affairs could not halt.

sentences.zh: 以清河王亶為大司馬，居尚書下舍而承制決事焉。

translations.literal: He made Prince Dan of Qinghe Grand Marshal, dwelling in the Secretariat's lower quarters to receive edicts and decide affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made Prince Dan of Qinghe Grand Marshal to decide affairs below the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王稱警蹕，神武醜之。

translations.literal: The prince called out his guard of honor; Shenwu found it ugly.
translations.idiomatic: The prince called out guards of honor; Shenwu despised it.

sentences.zh: 神武尋至弘農，遂西克潼關，執毛洪賓。

translations.literal: Shenwu soon reached Hongnong, then west took Tong Pass and seized Mao Hongbin.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Hongnong, took Tong Pass, and seized Mao Hongbin.

sentences.zh: 進軍長城，龍門都督薛崇禮降。

translations.literal: Advancing to the Long Wall, Longmen Director Xue Chongli surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At the Long Wall Xue Chongli surrendered.

sentences.zh: 神武退舍河東，命行臺尚書長史薛瑜守潼關。

translations.literal: Shenwu withdrew to camp east of the river and ordered Mobile Secretariat Chief Clerk Xue Yu to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He camped east of the river and ordered Xue Yu to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 大都督庫狄溫守封陵。

translations.literal: Grand Commander Kudili Wen held Fengling.
translations.idiomatic: Kudili Wen held Fengling.

sentences.zh: 於蒲津西岸築城守華州。

translations.literal: On the west bank of Pu Ford he built a city to hold Hua province.
translations.idiomatic: West of Pu Ford he built a city to hold Hua.

sentences.zh: 以薛紹宗為刺史。

translations.literal: He made Xue Shaozong governor.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xue Shaozong governor.

sentences.zh: 高昂行豫州事。

translations.literal: Gao Ang acted for Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ang acted for Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 神武自發晉陽至此，凡四十啟，魏帝皆不答。

translations.literal: From leaving Jinyang to here Shenwu sent forty memorials; the Wei emperor answered none.
translations.idiomatic: From Jinyang to here he sent forty memorials; none were answered.

sentences.zh: 九月庚寅，神武還至洛陽。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin of the ninth month Shenwu returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin of the ninth month he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 乃遣僧道榮奉表關中，又不答。

translations.literal: He then sent the monk Daorong with a memorial to Guanzhong; again no answer.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Daorong with a memorial to Guanzhong; again no answer.

sentences.zh: 乃集百寮沙門耆老，議所推立。

translations.literal: He then gathered the hundred officials, monks, and elders to debate whom to enthrone.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered officials, monks, and elders to choose an emperor.

sentences.zh: 以為自孝昌衰亂，國統中絕，神主靡依，昭穆失序。

translations.literal: They held that since Xiaochang's disorder the imperial line had been cut and the spirit lords had none to rely on; the ancestral temple was out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiaochang the line was cut and the temple was out of order.

sentences.zh: 永安以孝文為伯考。

translations.literal: Yongan took Xiaowen as uncle in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yongan made Xiaowen an uncle in the temple.

sentences.zh: 永熙遷孝明於夾室。

translations.literal: Yongxi moved Xiaoming to a side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi moved Xiaoming to a side chamber.

sentences.zh: 業喪祚短，職此之由。

translations.literal: Short reign and lost fortune came from this.
translations.idiomatic: Short reign came from this.

sentences.zh: 遂議立清河王世子善見。

translations.literal: They therefore resolved to enthrone Shan Jian, son of Prince Xuan of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: They resolved to enthrone Shan Jian, son of Prince Xuan of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 議定，白清河王。

translations.literal: When the decision was fixed they informed the Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: They informed the Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「天子無父，茍使兒立，不惜余生。

translations.literal: The prince said, "The Son of Heaven has no father; if you will set up my son, I do not begrudge the rest of my life."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "A Son of Heaven has no father; set up my son and I give my life gladly."

sentences.zh: 」乃立之，是為孝靜帝。

translations.literal: They enthroned him; this is Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned him as Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 魏於是始分為二。

translations.literal: Wei was thereby divided in two.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was divided in two.

sentences.zh: 神武以孝武既西，恐逼崤陜，洛陽復在河外，接近梁境。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because Xiaowu had gone west, feared pressure on the passes and that Luoyang, outside the river and near Liang territory,
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu had gone west; Luoyang lay outside the river near Liang.

sentences.zh: 如向晉陽，形勢不能相接。

translations.literal: if turned toward Jinyang, could not connect in posture,
translations.idiomatic: Turned toward Jinyang it could not connect.

sentences.zh: 依議遷鄴。

translations.literal: followed counsel to move the capital to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel moved the capital to Ye.

sentences.zh: 護軍祖瑩贊焉。

translations.literal: Protector Army Zu Ying praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ying praised the move.

sentences.zh: 詔下三日，車駕便發，戶四十萬，狼狽就道。

translations.literal: Three days after the edict the imperial carriage set out; four hundred thousand households went on the road in distress.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the court moved; four hundred thousand households fled in distress.

sentences.zh: 神武留洛陽部分，事畢還晉陽。

translations.literal: Shenwu remained at Luoyang to arrange affairs and then returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu arranged Luoyang and returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 自是軍國政務，皆歸相府。

translations.literal: From then on military and state affairs all went to the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Military and state affairs went to the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠曰：「可憐青雀子，飛來鄴城裏。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's song said, "Pity the green sparrow child, flying into Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: A song said, "Pity the green sparrow flying into Ye.

sentences.zh: 羽翮垂欲成，化作鸚鵡子。

translations.literal: Wings about to finish growing, it turns into a parrot child."
translations.idiomatic: Wings nearly grown, it turns into a parrot."

sentences.zh: 」好事者竊言，雀子謂魏帝清河王，鸚鵡謂神武也。

translations.literal: Those who delighted in such things whispered that sparrow meant the Wei emperor Prince of Qinghe and parrot meant Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wits said sparrow meant the Wei emperor and parrot meant Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 初，孝昌中，山胡劉蠡升自稱天子，年號神嘉，居雲陽谷。

translations.literal: Earlier in Xiaochang the mountain Hu Liu Lin Sheng styled himself Son of Heaven, era name Shenjia, and dwelt in Cloudyang Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang Liu Lin Sheng of the mountain Hu styled himself Son of Heaven at Cloudyang Valley.

sentences.zh: 西土歲被其寇，謂之胡荒。

translations.literal: The western lands were raided yearly; they called it Hu wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: The west was raided yearly; they called it Hu wasteland.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，西魏渭州刺史可朱渾道元擁眾內屬，神武迎納之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Western Wei Weizhou inspector Kezhuhun Daoyuan led his multitude to submit inward; Shenwu received him.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan of Weizhou submitted; Shenwu received him.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，神武襲擊劉蠡升，大破之。

translations.literal: On the day renxu Shenwu struck Liu Lin Sheng and broke him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he struck Lin Sheng and broke him.

sentences.zh: 己巳，魏帝褒詔，以神武為相國，假黃鉞，劍履上殿，入朝不趨。

translations.literal: On the day jisi the Wei emperor praised him in edict and made Shenwu Chancellor, acting Yellow Battle-Ax, sword and shoes in the hall, no hastening at court.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor made Shenwu chancellor with full honors.

sentences.zh: 神武固辭。

translations.literal: Shenwu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu declined.

sentences.zh: 三月，神武欲以女妻蠡升太子，候其不設備。

translations.literal: In the third month Shenwu wished to marry his daughter to Lin Sheng's crown prince and wait for him to be off guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he wished to marry his daughter to Lin Sheng's heir and catch him off guard.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，潛師襲之。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou he secretly struck.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he struck secretly.

sentences.zh: 其北部王斬蠡升首以送。

translations.literal: The northern king beheaded Lin Sheng and sent the head.
translations.idiomatic: The northern king beheaded Lin Sheng and sent the head.

sentences.zh: 其眾復立其子南海王。

translations.literal: The multitude again set up his son the Prince of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: The host set up his son the Prince of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 神武進擊之，又獲南海王，及其弟西海王、北海王、皇后、公卿已下四百餘人，胡、魏五萬戶。

translations.literal: Shenwu pressed the attack, again took the Prince of Nanhai and his brother the Princes of West Sea and North Sea, the empress, dukes and ministers below four hundred men, and fifty thousand Hu and Wei households.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Prince of Nanhai, his brothers, the empress, four hundred officials, and fifty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 壬申，神武朝於鄴。

translations.literal: On the day renshen Shenwu attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he attended court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 四月，神武請給遷人廩各有差。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Shenwu asked that migrants be given grain rations each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he asked grain rations for migrants.

sentences.zh: 九月甲寅，神武以州、郡、縣官多乖法，請出使問人疾苦。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin of the ninth month Shenwu, because provincial, commandery, and county officials often violated law, asked to send envoys to inquire into popular hardship.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin of the ninth month he asked envoys to inquire into hardship.

sentences.zh: 三年正月甲子，神武帥庫狄幹等萬騎襲西魏夏州。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi of the first month of the third year Shenwu led Kudili Gan and ten thousand horse in a surprise strike on Western Wei Xia province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the third year he led ten thousand horse against Xia province.

sentences.zh: 身不火食，四日而至。

translations.literal: He ate no cooked food for four days until he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He ate no cooked food for four days until arrival.

sentences.zh: 縛槊為悌，夜入其城。

translations.literal: He bound spears as ladders and entered the city by night.
translations.idiomatic: He bound spears as ladders and entered by night.

sentences.zh: 擒其刺史費也頭賀拔俄彌突，因而用之。

translations.literal: He seized the governor, the Feiyetou Heba Emitu, and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Governor Heba Emitu and employed him.

sentences.zh: 留都督張瓊以鎮守，遷其部落五千戶以歸。

translations.literal: He left Commander Zhang Qiong to hold it and moved five thousand households of the tribe back.
translations.idiomatic: He left Zhang Qiong to hold it and moved five thousand households back.

sentences.zh: 西魏靈州刺史曹泥，與其婿涼州刺史劉豐，遣使請內屬。

translations.literal: Western Wei Ling provincial inspector Cao Ni and his son-in-law Liang provincial inspector Liu Feng sent envoys asking to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ni and Liu Feng sent envoys asking to submit.

sentences.zh: 周文圍泥，水灌其城，不沒者四尺。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen besieged Ni; water flooded the city until only four feet were unsubmerged.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen flooded the city until only four feet remained dry.

sentences.zh: 神武命阿至羅發騎三萬，徑度靈州，繞出西軍後。

translations.literal: Shenwu ordered the Azhi-luo to send thirty thousand horse straight through Ling province and circle behind the western army.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu sent thirty thousand Azhi-luo horse around behind the western army.

sentences.zh: 獲馬五十匹。

translations.literal: They captured fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: They captured fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 西師乃退。

translations.literal: The western army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The western army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 神武率騎迎泥、豐生，拔其遺戶五千以歸，復泥官爵。

translations.literal: Shenwu led horse to meet Ni and Feng, brought back five thousand surviving households, and restored Ni's office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu met Ni and Feng, brought back five thousand households, and restored Ni's rank.

sentences.zh: 魏帝詔加神武九錫，固讓，乃止。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor edicted the nine bestowals on Shenwu; he firmly declined and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offered the nine bestowals; Shenwu declined.

sentences.zh: 二月，神武令阿至羅逼西魏秦州刺史建忠王万俟普撥，神武以眾應之。

translations.literal: In the second month Shenwu ordered the Azhi-luo to press Western Wei Qin provincial inspector Prince Jianzhong Wanqi Puba; Shenwu followed with the host.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he ordered the Azhi-luo against Puba; Shenwu followed with the host.

sentences.zh: 六月甲午，普撥與其子太宰受洛幹、豳州刺史叱干寶樂、右衛將軍破六韓常及督將三百餘人，擁部來降。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu of the sixth month Puba came with his son the Grand Preceptor Shouluogan, Binzhou inspector Chigan Baole, Right Guard General Poluhan Chang, and more than three hundred commanders and officers with their tribes to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu of the sixth month Puba and more than three hundred officers surrendered with their tribes.

sentences.zh: 八月丁亥，神武請均鬥尺，班於天下。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai of the eighth month Shenwu asked to standardize the dou and chi and distribute them through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai of the eighth month he standardized weights and measures for the realm.

sentences.zh: 九月辛亥，汾州胡王迢觸、曹貳龍聚眾反。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on the day xinhai the Fenzhou Hu Wang Yaochu and Cao Erlong gathered multitudes and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai of the ninth month Yaochu and Erlong rebelled.

sentences.zh: 署立百官，年號平都，神武討平之。

translations.literal: They set up officials and era name Pingdu; Shenwu pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: They named an era Pingdu; Shenwu pacified them.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁丑，神武自晉陽西討，遣兼僕射行臺、汝陽王暹、司徒高昂等趣上洛。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou of the twelfth month Shenwu campaigned west from Jinyang and sent Acting Palace Attendant Mobile Secretariat Prince Xian of Ruyang and Minister of Works Gao Ang toward Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he marched west and sent Prince Xian and Gao Ang toward Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 大都督竇泰入自潼關。

translations.literal: Grand Commander Dou Tai entered from Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai entered from Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 四年正月癸丑，竇泰軍敗自殺。

translations.literal: On the day guichou of the first month of the fourth year Dou Tai's army was defeated and he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Dou Tai's army was defeated and he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 神武軍次蒲津，以冰薄不得赴救。

translations.literal: Shenwu's army halted at Pu Ford; the ice was thin and he could not go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: At Pu Ford the ice was thin and he could not rescue.

sentences.zh: 乃班師。

translations.literal: He therefore withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高昂攻克上洛。

translations.literal: Gao Ang took Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ang took Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 二月乙酉，神武以並、肆、汾、建、晉、東雍、南汾、秦、陜九州霜旱，人饑流散，請所在開倉振給。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou of the second month Shenwu, because Bing, Si, Fen, Jian, Jin, Eastern Yong, Southern Fen, Qin, and Shaan nine provinces had frost and drought and people starved and scattered, asked that granaries be opened everywhere for relief.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he asked granaries opened in nine frost-stricken provinces.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申，神武如天池。

translations.literal: On the day renshen of the sixth month Shenwu went to Heaven Pool.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he went to Heaven Pool.

sentences.zh: 獲瑞石，隱起成文曰「六王三川」十一月壬辰，神武西討。

translations.literal: He obtained an auspicious stone with hidden raised writing saying "Six kings, three rivers." On the day renchen of the eleventh month he campaigned west.
translations.idiomatic: He found a stone marked "Six kings, three rivers." On renchen of the eleventh month he marched west.

sentences.zh: 自蒲津濟，眾二十萬。

translations.literal: He crossed at Pu Ford with two hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed at Pu Ford with two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 周文軍於沙苑。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen's army was at Sha Gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen camped at Sha Gardens.

sentences.zh: 神武以地厄少卻，西人鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because the ground was narrow, retreated slightly; the westerners drummed and shouted and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The ground was narrow; Shenwu retreated; the westerners shouted and advanced.

sentences.zh: 軍大亂，棄器甲十有八萬。

translations.literal: The army fell into great disorder and abandoned weapons and armor numbering one hundred eighty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The army broke and abandoned one hundred eighty thousand sets of arms.

sentences.zh: 神武跨駝，候船以歸。

translations.literal: Shenwu crossed a camel and waited for a boat to return.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu crossed on a camel and waited for a boat home.

sentences.zh: 元象元年三月辛酉，神武固請解丞相，魏帝許之。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou of the third month of Yuanxiang year one Shenwu firmly asked to resign the chancellorship; the Wei emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou of Yuanxiang year one he resigned the chancellorship; the emperor permitted.

sentences.zh: 四月庚寅，神武朝於鄴。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin of the fourth month Shenwu attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he attended court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day renchen he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 請開酒禁，並振恤宿衛武官。

translations.literal: He asked to lift the wine ban and relieve palace guard officers.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the wine ban and relieved guard officers.

sentences.zh: 七月壬午，行臺侯景、司徒高昂圍西魏將獨孤信於金墉。

translations.literal: On the day renwu of the seventh month Mobile Secretariat Hou Jing and Minister of Works Gao Ang besieged Western Wei general Dugu Xin at Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Hou Jing and Gao Ang besieged Dugu Xin at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 西魏帝及周文並來赴救。

translations.literal: The Western Wei emperor and Zhou Wen both came to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei emperor and Zhou Wen came to rescue.

sentences.zh: 大都督庫狄幹帥諸將前驅，神武總眾繼進。

translations.literal: Grand Commander Kudili Gan led the generals as vanguard; Shenwu followed with the whole host.
translations.idiomatic: Kudili Gan led the vanguard; Shenwu followed with the host.

sentences.zh: 八月辛卯，戰於河陰，大破西魏軍，俘獲數萬。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao of the eighth month they fought at Heyin and broke the Western Wei army utterly, capturing tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao at Heyin they broke the western army and took tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 司徒高昂、大都督李猛、宗顯死之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Gao Ang, Grand Commander Li Meng, and Zong Xian died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ang, Li Meng, and Zong Xian died.

sentences.zh: 西師之敗，獨孤信先入關，周文留其都督長孫子彥守金墉，遂燒營以遁。

translations.literal: In the western army's defeat Dugu Xin entered the passes first; Zhou Wen left his commander Sun Ziyan to hold Jinyong, then burned the camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin fled into the passes; Zhou Wen burned camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 神武遣兵追奔至崤，不及而還。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent troops in pursuit to Xiao but could not overtake them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuit reached Xiao but failed and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，神武知西師來侵，自晉陽率眾馳赴。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shenwu knew the western army would invade, he rushed from Jinyang with the host.
translations.idiomatic: When the western army invaded he rushed from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 至孟津，未濟，而軍有勝負。

translations.literal: At Meng Ford he had not yet crossed when the army had victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Meng Ford he had not crossed when fortune turned.

sentences.zh: 既而神武渡河，子彥亦棄城走。

translations.literal: After Shenwu crossed the river Ziyan also abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After he crossed, Ziyan abandoned the city.

sentences.zh: 神武遂毀金墉而還。

translations.literal: Shenwu then destroyed Jinyong and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed Jinyong and returned.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚午，神武朝於京師。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu of the eleventh month Shenwu attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he attended court.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬辰，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day renchen of the twelfth month he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 興和元年七月丁丑，魏帝進神武為相國、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou of the seventh month of Xinghe year one the Wei emperor promoted Shenwu to Chancellor and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou of Xinghe year one the emperor promoted him chancellor.

sentences.zh: 固讓，乃止。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He declined and it stopped.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙丑，神武以新宮成，朝於鄴。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the eleventh month, because the new palace was complete, Shenwu attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, with the new palace complete, he attended court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏帝與神武宴射，神武降階下稱賀。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor feasted and shot with Shenwu; Shenwu descended the steps and proclaimed congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted with him; Shenwu congratulated from below the steps.

sentences.zh: 又辭勃海王及都督中外諸軍事，詔不許。

translations.literal: He again declined Prince of Bohai and command of all armies within and without; the edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He declined Bohai and supreme command; the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊戌，神武還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu of the twelfth month Shenwu returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月，阿至羅別部遣使請降，神武帥眾迎之，出武州塞，不見。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year a separate branch of the Azhi-luo sent envoys asking to surrender; Shenwu led the host to meet them, went out Wuzhou pass, and did not see them.
translations.idiomatic: A branch of the Azhi-luo asked to surrender; he went out Wuzhou pass and did not see them.

sentences.zh: 大獵而還。

translations.literal: He held a great hunt and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted greatly and returned.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，神武巡北境，使使與蠕蠕通和。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year Shenwu inspected the northern frontier and sent envoys to treat with the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he inspected the north and treated with the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 四年五月辛巳，神武朝於鄴。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi of the fifth month of the fourth year Shenwu attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi of the fourth year he attended court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 請令百官，每月面敷政事。

translations.literal: He asked that the hundred officials each month face him and expound government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He asked officials to expound government monthly.

sentences.zh: 明揚仄陋，納諫屏邪。

translations.literal: Make clear the obscure and lowly; accept remonstrance and bar deceit.
translations.idiomatic: He sought talent and barred deceit.

sentences.zh: 親理獄訟，褒黜勤怠。

translations.literal: Personally judge lawsuits; reward diligence and punish slackness.
translations.idiomatic: He judged lawsuits and rewarded diligence.

sentences.zh: 牧守有愆，節級相坐。

translations.literal: If governors and magistrates were at fault, ranks were reduced in linked punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Faulty governors were punished in linked ranks.

sentences.zh: 椒掖之內，進禦以序。

translations.literal: Within the palace, consorts were presented in order.
translations.idiomatic: Palace consorts were presented in order.

sentences.zh: 後園鷹犬，悉皆棄之。

translations.literal: Hawks and hounds of the rear garden were all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Rear-garden hawks and hounds were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 六月甲辰，神武還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen of the sixth month Shenwu returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，神武西征。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Shenwu campaigned west.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he campaigned west.

sentences.zh: 十月己亥，圍西魏儀同三司王思政於玉壁城。

translations.literal: On the day jihai of the tenth month he besieged Western Wei Grand Opening Wang Sizheng at Yubi city.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he besieged Wang Sizheng at Yubi.

sentences.zh: 欲以致敵，西師不敢出。

translations.literal: He wished to draw the enemy; the western army did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to draw the enemy; the western army would not come out.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸未，神武以大雪，士卒多死，乃班師。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei of the eleventh month, because of great snow many soldiers died, he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei heavy snow killed many; he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 武定元年二月壬申，北豫州刺史高慎據武牢西叛。

translations.literal: On the day renshen of the second month of Wuding year one Northern Yuzhou inspector Gao Shen held Wulao and rebelled west.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Gao Shen held Wulao and rebelled west.

sentences.zh: 三月壬辰，周文率眾援高慎，圍河橋南城。

translations.literal: On the day renchen of the third month Zhou Wen led the host to aid Gao Shen and besieged the southern city of the River Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Zhou Wen besieged the River Bridge south city.

sentences.zh: 戊申，神武大敗之於芒山。

translations.literal: On the day wushen Shenwu greatly defeated him at Mang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he defeated Zhou Wen at Mang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 禽西魏督將以下四百餘人，俘斬六萬計。

translations.literal: He captured more than four hundred western commanders and officers below, and killed or captured sixty thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: He took four hundred officers and killed or captured sixty thousand.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍士有盜殺驢者，軍令應死。

translations.literal: At that time a soldier stole and killed a donkey; by military law he should die.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier killed a donkey; by law he should die.

sentences.zh: 神武弗殺，將至并州決之。

translations.literal: Shenwu did not kill him but was about to decide at Bingzhou the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu spared him for judgment at Bingzhou next day.

sentences.zh: 明日，復戰，奔西軍，告神武所在，西師盡銳來攻。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; he fled to the western army and told where Shenwu was; the western army came with full sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he fled to the western army and revealed Shenwu's position.

sentences.zh: 眾潰，神武失馬，赫連陽順下馬，以授神武，與蒼頭馮文洛扶上，俱走。

translations.literal: The multitude broke; Shenwu lost his horse; Helian Yangshun dismounted and gave his horse to Shenwu; with the servant Feng Wenluo supporting him they fled together.
translations.idiomatic: The host broke; Yangshun gave Shenwu his horse; he fled with Feng Wenluo.

sentences.zh: 從者步騎六七人。

translations.literal: Followers on foot and horse were six or seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven followers remained.

sentences.zh: 追騎至，親信都督尉興慶曰：「王去矣，興慶腰邊百箭，足殺百人。

translations.literal: Pursuing horse arrived; trusted commander Wei Xingqing said, "The king go; Xingqing has a hundred arrows at his waist, enough to kill a hundred men."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xingqing said, "Go, my lord; a hundred arrows will kill a hundred men."

sentences.zh: 」神武勉之曰：「事濟，以爾為懷州；

translations.literal: Shenwu urged him, "If the affair succeeds, I make you Governor of Huai;
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "Succeed and you are governor of Huai;

sentences.zh: 若死，則用爾子。」

translations.literal: if you die, I use your son."
translations.idiomatic: die and I use your son."

sentences.zh: 興慶曰：「兒小，願用兄。

translations.literal: Xingqing said, "My son is small; I wish to use my elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Xingqing said, "My son is small; use my brother."

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: He permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu permitted it.

sentences.zh: 興慶鬥，矢盡而死。

translations.literal: Xingqing fought until his arrows were spent and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqing fought until his arrows were spent and died.

sentences.zh: 西魏太師賀拔勝以十三騎逐神武，河州刺史劉洪徽射中其二。

translations.literal: Western Wei Grand Preceptor Heba Sheng pursued Shenwu with thirteen riders; Hezhou inspector Liu Honghui shot two of them down.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Sheng pursued with thirteen riders; Liu Honghui shot two down.

sentences.zh: 勝槊將中神武，段孝先橫射勝馬殪，遂免。

translations.literal: Sheng's spear was about to strike Shenwu when Duan Xiaoxian shot Sheng's horse dead crosswise and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiaoxian shot Sheng's horse dead and Shenwu was spared.

sentences.zh: 豫、洛二州平，神武使劉豐追奔徇地，至恒農而還。

translations.literal: Yu and Luo two provinces were pacified; Shenwu sent Liu Feng to pursue and sweep the land, reaching Hengnong and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Luo were pacified; Liu Feng pursued to Hengnong and returned.

sentences.zh: 七月，神武貽周文書，責以殺孝武之罪。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Shenwu sent a letter to Zhou Wen reproaching him for killing Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he reproached Zhou Wen for killing Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 八月辛未，魏帝詔神武為相國、錄尚書事、大行臺，余如故。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei of the eighth month the Wei emperor edicted Shenwu Chancellor, Director of the Secretariat, and Grand Mobile Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the emperor edicted him chancellor as before.

sentences.zh: 固辭，乃止。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He declined and it stopped.

sentences.zh: 是月，神武命於肆州北山築城，西自馬陵戍，東至土隥，四十日罷。

translations.literal: That month Shenwu ordered a wall built on the northern mountain of Si province from Maling garrison west to Tudi, finished in forty days.
translations.idiomatic: That month he built a wall on Si's northern mountain in forty days.

sentences.zh: 十二月己卯，神武朝於京師。

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the twelfth month Shenwu attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he attended court.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 二年三月癸巳，神武巡行冀、定二州，因朝京師。

translations.literal: On the day guisi of the second month of the second year Shenwu toured Ji and Ding provinces and attended court.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he toured Ji and Ding and attended court.

sentences.zh: 以冬春亢旱，請蠲縣責，振窮乏，宥死罪以下。

translations.literal: Because spring and winter were fiercely drought-stricken, he asked to remit county dues, relieve the poor, and pardon death crimes and below.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted dues, relieved the poor, and pardoned capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 又請授老人板職各有差。

translations.literal: He also asked to grant elders board offices each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He granted elders honorary offices by rank.

sentences.zh: 四月丙辰，神武還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen of the fourth month Shenwu returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，神武討山胡，破平之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Shenwu campaigned against the mountain Hu and broke and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he broke the mountain Hu.

sentences.zh: 俘獲一萬餘戶，分配諸州。

translations.literal: He captured more than ten thousand households and distributed them among the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He took ten thousand households and distributed them.

sentences.zh: 三年正月甲午，開府儀同三司爾朱文暢、開府司馬任胄、都督鄭仲禮、中府主簿李世林、前開府參軍房子遠等謀賊神武。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu of the third month Grand Opening Erzhu Wenchang, Opening Marshal Ren Zhou, Commander Zheng Zhongli, Secretariat clerk Li Shilin, and former Opening staff member Fang Ziyuan and others plotted to assassinate Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Wenchang, Ren Zhou, and others plotted to kill Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 因十五日夜打蔟，懷刃而入。

translations.literal: On the night of the fifteenth they beat clusters, entered with blades hidden.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth night they entered with hidden blades.

sentences.zh: 其黨薛季孝以告，並伏誅。

translations.literal: Their comrade Xue Jixiao informed; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jixiao informed; all were executed.

sentences.zh: 丁未，神武請於并州置晉陽宮，以處配口。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei Shenwu asked to build a Jinyang palace at Bingzhou for assigned households.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he asked a Jinyang palace for assigned households.

sentences.zh: 三月乙未，神武朝鄴。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei of the third month Shenwu attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei he attended Ye.

sentences.zh: 丙午，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 十月丁卯，神武上言，幽、安、定三州北接奚、蠕蠕，請於險要修立城戍以防之。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao of the tenth month Shenwu memorialized that You, An, and Ding three provinces bordered the Xi and Rouran in the north and asked to build frontier forts at dangerous points for defense.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he asked forts on the northern frontier of You, An, and Ding.

sentences.zh: 躬自臨履，莫不嚴固。

translations.literal: He personally went to inspect; none was not strict and solid.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected in person; every fort was strict.

sentences.zh: 乙未，神武請釋芒山俘桎梏，配以人間寡婦。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei Shenwu asked to release Mang Mountain prisoners from fetters and pair them with widows of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei he released Mang Mountain prisoners and paired them with widows.

sentences.zh: 四年八月癸巳，神武將西伐，自鄴會兵於晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day guisi of the eighth month of the fourth year Shenwu was about to campaign west and assembled troops at Jinyang from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi of the eighth month he assembled at Jinyang for the west.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍曹魏祖曰：「不可，今八月西方王，以死氣逆生氣，為客不利，主人則可。

translations.literal: Palace General Wei Chaozu said, "You must not; in the eighth month the western king reigns; using dead qi against living qi, the guest is unlucky while the host may succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chaozu warned: August favors the west; the guest will lose.

sentences.zh: 兵果行，傷大將。

translations.literal: If troops go, a great general will be wounded."
translations.idiomatic: March and a great general will be wounded."

sentences.zh: 」神武不從。

translations.literal: Shenwu did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu refused.

sentences.zh: 自東西魏構兵，鄴下每先有黃黑螘陣鬥。

translations.literal: From the time Eastern and Western Wei contended, below Ye there were often swarms of yellow and black ants fighting first.
translations.idiomatic: After the split, yellow and black ant swarms fought below Ye.

sentences.zh: 占者以為黃者東魏戎衣色，黑者西魏戎衣色，人間以此候勝負。

translations.literal: Diviners held yellow to be Eastern Wei battle dress and black Western Wei battle dress; people used this to foretell victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow meant Eastern Wei, black Western Wei; people read victory in the ants.

sentences.zh: 是時黃螘盡死。

translations.literal: At this time the yellow ants all died.
translations.idiomatic: Now the yellow ants all died.

sentences.zh: 九月，神武圍玉壁以挑西師，不敢應。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Shenwu besieged Yubi to challenge the western army; it did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he besieged Yubi; the western army would not answer.

sentences.zh: 西魏晉州刺史韋孝寬守玉壁。

translations.literal: Western Wei Jin provincial inspector Wei Xiaokuan held Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan held Yubi.

sentences.zh: 城中出鐵面。

translations.literal: The city produced iron masks.
translations.idiomatic: The city used iron masks.

sentences.zh: 神武使兀盜射之，每中其目。

translations.literal: Shenwu sent the archer Wudao to shoot; each shot hit the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Archer Wudao shot; each arrow found an eye.

sentences.zh: 用李業興孤虛術，萃其北。

translations.literal: Using Li Yexing's solitary void method, he massed against the north.
translations.idiomatic: By Li Yexing's method he massed against the north.

sentences.zh: 北，天險也。

translations.literal: North is heaven's danger.
translations.idiomatic: North is heaven's danger.

sentences.zh: 乃起土山，鑿十道。

translations.literal: He then raised earthen hills and dug ten tunnels.
translations.idiomatic: He raised earthworks and dug ten tunnels.

sentences.zh: 又於東面鑿二十一道，以攻之。

translations.literal: Also on the east face he dug twenty-one tunnels to attack.
translations.idiomatic: On the east he dug twenty-one tunnels.

sentences.zh: 城中無水，汲於汾。

translations.literal: The city had no water and drew from the Fen.
translations.idiomatic: The city had no water and drew from the Fen.

sentences.zh: 神武使移汾，一夜而畢。

translations.literal: Shenwu had the Fen diverted; it was done in one night.
translations.idiomatic: He diverted the Fen in one night.

sentences.zh: 孝寬奪據土山。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan seized the earthen hills.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan seized the earthworks.

sentences.zh: 頓軍五旬，城不拔，死者七萬人，聚為一冢。

translations.literal: The army halted five weeks; the city was not taken; seventy thousand died and were heaped in one mound.
translations.idiomatic: Five weeks passed; the city held; seventy thousand died in one mound.

sentences.zh: 有星墜於神武營，眾驢並鳴，士皆懾懼。

translations.literal: A star fell in Shenwu's camp; the multitude of donkeys brayed together; soldiers were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: A star fell in camp; donkeys brayed; soldiers feared.

sentences.zh: 神武有疾。

translations.literal: Shenwu fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu fell ill.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚子，輿疾班師。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi of the eleventh month he led the sick army back.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he withdrew with the sick army.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，遣太原公洋鎮鄴。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu he sent Prince of Taiyuan Yang to hold Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu he sent Prince Yang to hold Ye.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，征世子澄至晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai he summoned the heir Cheng to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he summoned the heir Cheng to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 有惡鳥集於亭樹，世子使斛律光射殺之。

translations.literal: Evil birds gathered in the pavilion trees; the heir had Hulu Guang shoot them dead.
translations.idiomatic: Evil birds gathered; the heir had Hulu Guang shoot them.

sentences.zh: 己卯，神武以無功，表解都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On the day jimao Shenwu, because there was no achievement, memorialized to resign command of all armies within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he resigned supreme command for lack of success.

sentences.zh: 魏帝優詔許焉。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor issued a gracious edict permitting it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor permitted it.

sentences.zh: 是時，西魏言神武中弩。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Wei said Shenwu had been hit by a crossbow bolt.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei said Shenwu was wounded by a bolt.

sentences.zh: 神武聞之，乃勉坐見諸貴。

translations.literal: When Shenwu heard it he forced himself to sit and receive the nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this he forced himself to receive the nobles.

sentences.zh: 使斛律金敕勒歌，神武自和之，哀感流涕。

translations.literal: He had Hulu Jin sing the Chile song; Shenwu harmonized with it and wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He had Hulu Jin sing; Shenwu harmonized and wept.

sentences.zh: 侯景素輕世子，嘗謂司馬子如曰：「王在，吾不敢有異。

translations.literal: Hou Jing had long looked down on the heir; he once told Sima Ziru, "While the king lives I dare not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing despised the heir and told Ziru, "While the king lives I dare not differ.

sentences.zh: 王無，吾不能與鮮卑小兒共事。

translations.literal: When the king is gone I cannot serve a Xianbei boy."
translations.idiomatic: When the king is gone I will not serve a Xianbei boy."

sentences.zh: 」子如掩其口。

translations.literal: Ziru covered his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru covered his mouth.

sentences.zh: 至是，世子為神武書，召景。

translations.literal: Now the heir wrote for Shenwu summoning Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The heir wrote summoning Jing for Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 景先與神武約，得書，書背微點，乃來。

translations.literal: Jing had agreed with Shenwu that when a letter came, a faint dot on the back meant come.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Shenwu agreed: a dot on the back meant come.

sentences.zh: 書至，無點，景不至。

translations.literal: The letter arrived without a dot; Jing did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The letter had no dot; Jing did not come.

sentences.zh: 又聞神武疾，遂擁兵自固。

translations.literal: Hearing Shenwu was ill, he then held troops and secured himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Shenwu was ill, Jing secured himself with troops.

sentences.zh: 神武謂世子曰：「我雖疾，爾面更有餘憂色，何也？

translations.literal: Shenwu told the heir, "Though I am ill, your face has still more worry; why?
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu asked the heir, "I am ill, yet you look more worried; why?

sentences.zh: 」世子未對。

translations.literal: The heir did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The heir did not answer.

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「豈非憂侯景叛邪？」

translations.literal: He asked again, "Is it not worry that Hou Jing will rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "Do you fear Hou Jing will rebel?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「然。

translations.literal: He said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「景專制河南十四年矣，常有飛揚跋扈誌。

translations.literal: Shenwu said, "Jing has held Henan autonomously for fourteen years and often had overbearing intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "Jing held Henan fourteen years with overbearing intent.

sentences.zh: 顧我能養，豈為汝駕御也。

translations.literal: Considering I could still nourish him, how could he be driven by you?
translations.idiomatic: While I lived he obeyed me; he will not obey you.

sentences.zh: 今四方未定，勿遽發哀。

translations.literal: The four quarters are not yet settled; do not hasten to announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is unsettled; do not hasten mourning.

sentences.zh: 庫狄幹鮮卑老公，斛律金敕勒老公，並性遒直，終不負汝。

translations.literal: Kudili Gan is an old Xianbei man, Hulu Jin an old Chile man; both are upright by nature and in the end will not fail you.
translations.idiomatic: Kudili Gan and Hulu Jin are upright and will not fail you.

sentences.zh: 可朱渾道元、劉豐生遠來投我，必無異心。

translations.literal: Kezhuhun Daoyuan and Liu Feng came from afar to join me; surely they have no other heart.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan and Liu Feng came from afar; they are loyal.

sentences.zh: 賀拔焉過兒樸實無罪過，潘相樂今本作道人，心和厚，汝兄弟當得其力。

translations.literal: Heba Yaguor is plain and without fault; Pan Xiangle is kind and thick-hearted; you brothers should gain their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yaguor is plain; Pan Xiangle is kind; use them.

sentences.zh: 韓軌少戇，宜寬借之。

translations.literal: Han Gui is young and blunt; you should treat him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gui is young and blunt; treat him generously.

sentences.zh: 彭相樂心腹難得，宜防護之。

translations.literal: Peng Xiangle is hard to win as confidant; you should guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Xiangle is hard to trust; guard against him.

sentences.zh: 少堪敵侯景者，唯有慕容紹宗。

translations.literal: Few can match Hou Jing; only Murong Shaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Only Murong Shaozong can match Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 我故不貴之，留以與汝，宜深加殊禮，委以經略。

translations.literal: I therefore did not ennoble him and left him for you; you should honor him exceptionally and entrust strategy to him.
translations.idiomatic: I left Shaozong for you; honor him and entrust strategy.

sentences.zh: 五年正月朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the fifth year there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's day the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「日蝕其為我邪？

translations.literal: Shenwu said, "The eclipse is for me?
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "Is the eclipse for me?

sentences.zh: 死亦何恨。

translations.literal: To die is nothing to regret."
translations.idiomatic: Death is nothing to regret."

sentences.zh: 」丙午，陳啟於魏帝。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu he reported illness to the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he reported illness to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 是日，崩於晉陽，時年五十二。

translations.literal: That day he died at Jinyang, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: That day he died at Jinyang, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 秘不發喪。

translations.literal: Death was kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Death was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 六月壬午，魏帝於東堂舉哀三日。

translations.literal: On the day renwu of the sixth month the Wei emperor mourned at the Eastern Hall for three days.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu of the sixth month the emperor mourned three days.

sentences.zh: 制緦衰，詔凶禮依漢大將軍霍光、東平王蒼故事。

translations.literal: He ordered hemp mourning; funeral rites followed Han Grand General Huo Guang and Prince Cang of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral rites followed Huo Guang and Prince Cang of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、使持節、相國、都督中外諸軍事、齊王璽紱、辌車、黃屋左纛、前後羽葆鼓吹、輕車介士、兼備九錫殊禮。

translations.literal: Bestowed acting Yellow Battle-Ax, credentials, chancellor, command of all armies, Qi king's seal and ribbon, imperial carriage, yellow canopy left pennon, guards before and behind, light chariot guard, and the full nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: He received the full nine bestowals and honors.

sentences.zh: 謚獻武王。

translations.literal: Posthumous title King Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title King Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 八月甲申，葬於鄴西北漳水之西，魏帝臨送於紫陽。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the eighth month he was buried west of the Zhang west of Ye; the Wei emperor attended the send-off at Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he was buried west of the Zhang; the emperor attended at Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 天保初，追崇為獻武帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was further honored as Emperor Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao he was honored as Emperor Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 廟號太祖，陵曰義平。

translations.literal: Temple name Taizu; tomb Yiping.
translations.idiomatic: Temple name Taizu; tomb Yiping.

sentences.zh: 天統元年，改謚神武皇帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiantong the posthumous title was changed to Emperor Shenwu; temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiantong he became Emperor Shenwu, temple Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 神武性深密高岸，終日儼然，人不能測。

translations.literal: Shenwu's nature was deep, secret, lofty, and stern all day; men could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu was deep, secret, and stern; men could not fathom him.

sentences.zh: 機權之際，變化若神。

translations.literal: At moments of stratagem he changed like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In stratagem he changed like a spirit.

sentences.zh: 至於軍國大略，獨運懷抱。

translations.literal: As to grand strategy of army and state he carried it alone in his breast.
translations.idiomatic: Grand strategy of army and state he carried alone.

sentences.zh: 文武將吏，罕有預之。

translations.literal: Civil and military officers rarely shared in it.
translations.idiomatic: Officers rarely shared in it.

sentences.zh: 經馭軍眾，法令嚴肅，臨敵制勝，策出無方。

translations.literal: In commanding armies his laws were strict; facing the enemy he conquered; plans came from nowhere.
