translations.idiomatic: His laws were strict; facing enemies he won; plans seemed from nowhere.

sentences.zh: 聽斷昭察，不可欺犯，知人好士，全護勛舊。

translations.literal: In hearing and deciding he was clear and could not be deceived; he knew men and loved scholars; he fully protected those with merit of old.
translations.idiomatic: He judged clearly, loved talent, and protected old merit.

sentences.zh: 性周給，每有文教，常殷勤款悉。

translations.literal: His nature was generous in all directions; whenever there was civil teaching he was earnest and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous and earnest in civil teaching.

sentences.zh: 指事論心，不尚綺靡。

translations.literal: He spoke to the matter and discussed the heart, not fond of ornate flourish.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke to the heart, not to ornament.

sentences.zh: 擢人授任，在於得才。

translations.literal: In raising men and giving office what mattered was obtaining talent.
translations.idiomatic: In office what mattered was talent.

sentences.zh: 茍其所堪，乃至拔於廝養；

translations.literal: If they were capable he would raise them even from stable boys;
translations.idiomatic: He raised even stable boys if they were capable;

sentences.zh: 有虛聲無實者，稀見任用。

translations.literal: those with empty fame and no substance he rarely employed.
translations.idiomatic: empty fame he rarely employed.

sentences.zh: 諸將出討，奉行方略，罔不克捷。

translations.literal: When generals went on campaign they followed the plan and none failed to triumph.
translations.idiomatic: Generals who followed his plans triumphed.

sentences.zh: 違失指畫，多致奔亡。

translations.literal: Those who missed his direction mostly fled and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who missed his direction perished.

sentences.zh: 雅尚儉素，刀劍鞍勒無金玉之飾。

translations.literal: He esteemed plainness; swords, saddles, and bridles had no gold or jade ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He loved plainness; arms bore no gold or jade.

sentences.zh: 少能劇飲，自當大任，不過三爵。

translations.literal: In youth he could drink heavily; once he bore great responsibility he did not exceed three cups.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he drank deep; in power he stopped at three cups.

sentences.zh: 居家如官。

translations.literal: At home he was as at office.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was as at office.

sentences.zh: 仁恕愛士。

translations.literal: He was benevolent, forgiving, and loved scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He was benevolent and loved scholars.

sentences.zh: 始范陽盧景裕以明經稱，魯郡韓毅以工書顯，咸以謀逆見禽，並蒙恩置之第館，教授諸子。

translations.literal: Once Lu Jingyu of Fanyang was famed for classics and Han Yi of Lu for calligraphy; both were seized for plotting rebellion yet received favor, housed in mansions, and taught his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingyu and Han Yi, seized for treason, were housed and taught his sons.

sentences.zh: 其文武之士，盡節所事見執獲而不罪者甚多。

translations.literal: Of civil and military men who served faithfully yet were captured, many were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Many captured loyalists were not punished.

sentences.zh: 故遐邇歸心，皆思效力。

translations.literal: Therefore near and far gave their hearts and all wished to serve his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far gave their hearts and wished to serve.

sentences.zh: 至南和梁國，北懷蠕蠕。

translations.literal: South he harmonized Liang; north he cherished the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: South he won Liang; north he won the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾、阿至羅咸所招納，獲其力用，規略遠矣。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun and the Azhi-luo were all won over and their strength used; his strategy reached far.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun and the Azhi-luo were won and used; his reach was far.

sentences.zh: 世宗文襄皇帝諱澄，字子惠，神武長子也。

translations.literal: Shizong Emperor Wenxiang, taboo name Cheng, courtesy name Zihui, was Shenwu's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong Emperor Wenxiang, taboo Cheng, courtesy Zihui, was Shenwu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰婁太后。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Dowager Lou.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Dowager Lou.

sentences.zh: 生而岐嶷，神武異之。

translations.literal: Born with exceptional intelligence, Shenwu marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Born gifted, Shenwu marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 魏中興元年，立為勃海王世子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing of Wei he was established heir to the Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongxing year one he was made heir to the Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 就杜詢講學，敏悟過人，詢甚嘆服。

translations.literal: He studied with Du Xun; his quick perception surpassed others and Xun sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with Du Xun and surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 二年，加侍中、開府儀同三司，尚孝靜帝妹馮翊長公主。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Opening with the same third rank and married the Emperor Xiaojing's sister the Princess of Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he became Palace Attendant and married the Princess of Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 時年十二，神情俊爽，便若成人。

translations.literal: At age twelve his spirit and manner were handsome and clear, already like a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he seemed already a man.

sentences.zh: 神武試問以時事得失，辨析無不中理。

translations.literal: Shenwu tested him on the gains and losses of the times; his analysis never missed the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu tested him on affairs of the day; he never missed.

sentences.zh: 自是軍國籌策皆預之。

translations.literal: From then on he took part in all military and state planning.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he joined all military and state planning.

sentences.zh: 天平元年，加使持節、尚書令、大行臺、并州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianping he was made credential-holder, Director of the Secretariat, Grand Mobile Secretariat, and Bing provincial inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year one he became Director of the Secretariat and inspector of Bing.

sentences.zh: 三年，入輔朝政，加領軍左右、京畿大都督。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered to assist court governance and was further made Commander of the Guards and Grand Commander of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he assisted court and commanded the capital guards.

sentences.zh: 時人雖聞器識，猶以少年期之。

translations.literal: People of the time though they heard of his talent still expected him as a youth.
translations.idiomatic: Men heard his talent yet still judged him a youth.

sentences.zh: 而機略嚴明，事無疑滯，於是朝野振肅。

translations.literal: Yet his stratagems were strict and bright and affairs never stalled; court and country were shaken into order.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his counsel was sharp and affairs never stalled; the court was awed into order.

sentences.zh: 元象元年，攝吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he acted as Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang year one he acted as Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 魏自崔亮以後，選人常以年勞為制。

translations.literal: Since Cui Liang of Wei, selection had often followed years of service as rule.
translations.idiomatic: Since Cui Liang, selection followed years of service.

sentences.zh: 文襄乃厘改前式，銓擢唯在得人。

translations.literal: Wenxiang then reformed the former style; promotion and selection rested only on obtaining the right man.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang reformed the system; promotion rested on merit alone.

sentences.zh: 又沙汰尚書郎，妙選人地以充之。

translations.literal: He also sifted Secretariat gentlemen and finely chose men of quality and locality to fill posts.
translations.idiomatic: He sifted Secretariat gentlemen and chose men of quality.

sentences.zh: 至於才名之士，咸被薦擢。

translations.literal: Men of talent and fame were all recommended and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent and fame were promoted.

sentences.zh: 假有未居顯位者，皆致之門下，以為賓客。

translations.literal: If some had not yet reached high office they were brought to his gate as guests.
translations.idiomatic: Those not yet in high office he kept as guests.

sentences.zh: 每山園遊宴，必見招攜；

translations.literal: Whenever he toured gardens and feasted he was sure to summon them;
translations.idiomatic: At garden feasts he summoned them;

sentences.zh: 執射賦詩，各盡其所長，以為娛適。

translations.literal: shooting arrows and composing verse, each showing his strength, for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: they shot and composed verse for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 興和二年，加大將軍，領中書監，仍攝吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xinghe he was made Grand General, Director of the Secretariat, and still acted as Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe year two he became Grand General and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自正光已後，天下多事。

translations.literal: Since Zhenguang the realm had many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhenguang the realm had known trouble.

sentences.zh: 在任群官，廉潔者寡。

translations.literal: Of officials in office, few were clean.
translations.idiomatic: Few officials were clean.

sentences.zh: 文襄乃奏吏部郎崔暹為御史中尉，糾劾權豪，無所縱舍。

translations.literal: Wenxiang then memorialized Personnel Gentleman Cui Xian as Censorate Director to impeach powerful families without indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: He made Cui Xian censor and impeached the powerful without mercy.

sentences.zh: 於是風俗更始，私枉路絕。

translations.literal: Customs were thereby renewed and private wrongs on the road ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Customs renewed; private wrongs ceased.

sentences.zh: 乃榜於街衢，具論經國政術，仍開直言之路。

translations.literal: He posted notices in the streets expounding statecraft and opened the way for blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: He posted statecraft in the streets and opened blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 有論事上書苦言切至者，皆優容之。

translations.literal: Those who memorialized with bitter, cutting words were all treated generously.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter memorialists were treated generously.

sentences.zh: 武定四年十一月，神武西討，不豫，班師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Wuding Shenwu campaigned west, fell ill, and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding year four Shenwu campaigned west, fell ill, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 文襄馳赴軍所，侍衛還晉陽。

translations.literal: Wenxiang galloped to the army, attended him, and returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang galloped to the army and returned with him to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 五年正月丙午，神武崩，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu of the first month of the fifth year Shenwu died; death was kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu of the fifth year Shenwu died; death was secret.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，司徒侯景據河南反，潁州刺史司馬世雲以城應之。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai Minister of Works Hou Jing held Henan and rebelled; Ying provincial inspector Sima Shiyun opened the city in response.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Hou Jing rebelled in Henan; Sima Shiyun opened Ying.

sentences.zh: 景誘執豫州刺史高元成、襄州刺史李密、廣州刺史暴顯等。

translations.literal: Jing enticed and seized Yuzhou inspector Gao Yuancheng, Xiangzhou inspector Li Mi, and Guangzhou inspector Bao Xian and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jing seized Yuancheng, Li Mi, Bao Xian, and others.

sentences.zh: 遣司空韓軌率眾討之。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of Works Han Gui to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Han Gui against him.

sentences.zh: 四月壬申，文襄朝於鄴。

translations.literal: On the day renshen of the fourth month Wenxiang attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Wenxiang attended court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，韓軌等自潁州班師。

translations.literal: On the day jisi of the sixth month Han Gui and others withdrew from Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Han Gui withdrew from Ying.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，文襄還晉陽，乃發喪，告喻文武，陳神武遺誌。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou Wenxiang returned to Jinyang, then announced mourning, informed civil and military, and stated Shenwu's last will.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he returned to Jinyang, announced mourning, and stated the last will.

sentences.zh: 七月戊戌，魏帝詔以文襄為使持節、大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、大行臺、勃海王。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu of the seventh month the Wei emperor edicted Wenxiang credential-holder, Grand Chancellor, commander of all armies, Director of the Secretariat, Grand Mobile Secretariat, Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor made Wenxiang chancellor and Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 文襄啟辭位，願停王爵。

translations.literal: Wenxiang memorialized declining office and wished to stop the princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang declined and wished to stop the princely rank.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏帝詔太原公洋攝理軍國，遣中使敦喻。

translations.literal: On the day renyin the Wei emperor edicted Prince of Taiyuan Yang to administer army and state and sent palace envoys to urge him.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the emperor set Prince Yang to administer state and urged him.

sentences.zh: 八月戊辰，文襄啟申神武遺令，請減國邑，分封將督各有差。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen of the eighth month Wenxiang memorialized Shenwu's last order asking to reduce the state fief and enfeoff generals each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he asked to reduce the fief and reward generals.

sentences.zh: 辛未，朝於鄴，固辭丞相。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei he attended court at Ye and firmly declined the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he attended Ye and declined the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 魏帝詔曰：「既朝野攸憑，安危所系，不得令遂本懷，須有權奪。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor edicted, "Court and country rely on you; safety and danger hang on you; I cannot let your original wish stand; there must be temporary seizure of power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said court and realm relied on him and refused his decline.

sentences.zh: 可復前大將軍，余如故。

translations.literal: You may resume former Grand General; the rest as before."
translations.idiomatic: Resume Grand General; the rest as before."

sentences.zh: 」壬辰，尚書祠部郎中元瑾、梁降人茍濟、長秋卿劉思逸及淮南王宣洪、華山王大器、濟北王徽等謀害文襄，事發伏誅。

translations.literal: On the day renchen Secretariat Sacrifices Gentleman Yuan Jin, Liang surrenderer Gou Ji, Chief of the Long Autumn Liu Siyi, Prince Xuanhong of Huainan, Prince Daqi of Huashan, Prince Hui of Jibei and others plotted to harm Wenxiang; the affair broke and they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Yuan Jin, Gou Ji, Liu Siyi, and princes plotted against Wenxiang and were executed.

sentences.zh: 九月己亥，文襄請舊勛灼然未蒙齒錄者，悉求旌賞。

translations.literal: On the day jihai of the ninth month Wenxiang asked that old merit clearly not yet recorded all seek reward.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he asked reward for old merit not yet recorded.

sentences.zh: 朝士名行有聞，或以年耆疾滿告謝者，準其本秩。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen of name and conduct, or those who resigned through age or illness, kept their original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Men of name who resigned kept rank.

sentences.zh: 授以州郡，不得蒞事，聽廕子孫。

translations.literal: They were given provinces and commanderies but did not take office; sons and grandsons were enfeoffed in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: They received provinces in name; sons held office.

sentences.zh: 自天平元年以來，遇事亡官者，聽復本資。

translations.literal: From Tianping year one, those who lost office in affairs might restore original salary.
translations.idiomatic: From Tianping year one office-losers might restore salary.

sentences.zh: 豪貴之家，不得占護山澤。

translations.literal: Great and noble houses might not monopolize mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Great houses might not monopolize mountains and marshes.

sentences.zh: 其第宇車服婚姻送葬奢僭無限者，並令禁斷。

translations.literal: Those whose mansions, carriages, dress, marriage, and funerals exceeded limit were all forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Excess in mansions, dress, and funerals was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 從太昌元年以來，將帥有殊功異效者，其子弟年十歲以上，請聽依第出身。

translations.literal: From Taichang year one, generals of special merit, their sons ten years and above might enter office by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of meritorious generals might enter office by rank.

sentences.zh: 其兵士從征，身殞陣場者，蠲其家租課。

translations.literal: Soldiers who died in battle had household rent and dues remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Families of soldiers dead in battle were remitted rent.

sentences.zh: 若有藏器避世者，以禮招致，隨才擢敘。

translations.literal: If any hid talent and avoided the world they were welcomed by ritual and promoted according to ability.
translations.idiomatic: Recluses were welcomed and promoted by ability.

sentences.zh: 罷營構之官。

translations.literal: Construction offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Construction offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 在朝百司，怠惰不勤，有所曠廢者，免所居官。

translations.literal: Of the hundred offices at court, those idle and not diligent, neglecting duty, were removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Idle officials were removed.

sentences.zh: 若清幹克濟，皎然可知者，即宜超敘，不拘常式。

translations.literal: If pure and able and clearly known, they should be promoted beyond the usual rule.
translations.idiomatic: The pure and able were promoted beyond rule.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，文襄還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou Wenxiang returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 武定六年正月己未，文襄朝於鄴。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei of the first month of the sixth year of Wuding Wenxiang attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei of Wuding year six he attended Ye.

sentences.zh: 二月己卯，梁遣使慰文襄，並請通和。

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the second month Liang sent envoys to comfort Wenxiang and also asked for peace.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Liang sent envoys and asked peace.

sentences.zh: 文襄許其和而不答書。

translations.literal: Wenxiang permitted peace but did not reply in writing.
translations.idiomatic: He permitted peace but did not reply.

sentences.zh: 侯景之叛也，南兗州刺史石長宣頗相影響，諸州刺史、守、令、佐史多被詿誤。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Southern Yanzhou inspector Shi Changxuan was much influenced; many provincial inspectors, magistrates, and clerks were misled.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing rebelled many officials were misled.

sentences.zh: 景破後，悉被禽獲，尚書咸處極刑，文襄並請減降。

translations.literal: After Jing was broken all were captured; the Secretariat all sentenced extreme punishment; Wenxiang asked reduction for all.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing fell the Secretariat sought extreme punishment; Wenxiang asked mercy.

sentences.zh: 於是斬長宣，其餘並從寬宥。

translations.literal: Thereupon Changxuan was beheaded; the rest received broad pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Changxuan was beheaded; the rest were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三月戊申，文襄請朝臣及牧、守、令、長各舉賢良及驍武膽略堪守邊城者，務在得才，不拘職素。

translations.literal: On the day wushen Wenxiang asked court ministers and governors, magistrates, and chiefs each to recommend the worthy and the brave fit for frontier defense; what mattered was obtaining talent, not office category.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he asked all to recommend talent for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其稱事六品、散官五品以上，朝廷所悉，不在舉限。

translations.literal: Those of sixth rank and above and fifth-rank scattered office known to court were outside the recommendation limit.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and above were outside the limit.

sentences.zh: 其稱事七品、散官六品以下，並及州、郡、縣雜白身，不限在官、解職，並任舉之，隨才進擢。

translations.literal: Seventh rank and below, and miscellaneous commoners of provinces, commanderies, and counties, whether in office or dismissed, might all be recommended and promoted by ability.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank and below and commoners might all be recommended.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，文襄南臨黎陽，濟於武牢。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai Wenxiang went south to Liyang and crossed at Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he went south to Liyang and crossed at Wulao.

sentences.zh: 自洛陽，從太行而反晉陽。

translations.literal: From Luoyang he returned to Jinyang by the Taihang route.
translations.idiomatic: From Luoyang he returned to Jinyang by Taihang.

sentences.zh: 於路遺書朝士，以相戒厲。

translations.literal: On the road he left letters to court gentlemen as warning and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he wrote letters admonishing the court.

sentences.zh: 於是朝野承風，莫不震肅。

translations.literal: Thereupon court and country received the wind; none was not shaken into order.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country were shaken into order.

sentences.zh: 六月，文襄巡北邊城戍，振賜各有差。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Wenxiang inspected northern frontier forts; rewards each had differences.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he inspected northern forts and rewarded each.

sentences.zh: 七月乙卯，文襄朝於鄴。

translations.literal: On the day yimao of the seventh month Wenxiang attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he attended Ye.

sentences.zh: 八月庚寅，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin of the eighth month he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 使大行臺慕容紹宗與太尉高嶽、大都督劉豐討王思政於潁川。

translations.literal: He sent Grand Mobile Secretariat Murong Shaozong with Grand Commandant Gao Yue and Grand Commander Liu Feng to campaign against Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shaozong, Yue, and Feng against Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，文襄遣行臺尚書辛術率諸將略江淮之北。

translations.literal: Earlier Wenxiang had sent Mobile Secretariat Director Xin Shu with generals to sweep north of the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xin Shu had swept north of the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 至是，凡所獲二十三州。

translations.literal: By now what was taken totaled twenty-three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: By now twenty-three provinces had been taken.

sentences.zh: 七年四月甲辰，魏帝進文襄位相國，封齊王，綠綟綬。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen of the seventh month of the seventh year the Wei emperor promoted Wenxiang to Chancellor, enfeoffed him Prince of Qi with green ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the emperor made him Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 贊拜不名，入朝不趨，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: Praise without naming, no hastening at court, sword and shoes in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He received praise without naming, no hastening at court, and sword in the hall.

sentences.zh: 食冀州之勃海、長樂、安德、武邑、瀛州之河間五郡，邑十五萬戶，使持節、都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書、大行臺並如故。

translations.literal: Food from Bohai, Changle, Ande, and Wuyi of Ji and Hejian of Ying five commanderies, fief one hundred fifty thousand households; credentials and command of all armies as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fief of five commanderies and one hundred fifty thousand households; command as before.

sentences.zh: 丁未，文襄入朝。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei Wenxiang entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he entered court.

sentences.zh: 固讓，魏帝不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined; the Wei emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He declined; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 五月戊寅，文襄帥師自鄴赴潁川。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin of the fifth month Wenxiang led troops from Ye to Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he led troops to Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 六月丙申克潁川，禽西魏大將軍王思政，以忠於所事，釋而待之。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen of the sixth month he took Yingchuan and captured Western Wei Grand General Wang Sizheng; because he was loyal to his charge he released and treated him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he took Yingchuan and spared the loyal Wang Sizheng.

sentences.zh: 七月，文襄朝於鄴，請魏帝立皇太子，復辭爵位殊禮，未報。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wenxiang attended court at Ye and asked the Wei emperor to establish a crown prince; he again declined special rank; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he asked for a crown prince and declined special rank.

sentences.zh: 八月辛卯，遇盜而崩。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao of the eighth month he met robbers and died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he was slain by robbers.

sentences.zh: 初，梁將蘭欽子京見虜，文襄以配廚。

translations.literal: Earlier Liang general Lan Qin's son Jing was captured; Wenxiang assigned him to the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Liang general Lan Qin's son Jing was captured and assigned to the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 欽求贖之，不許。

translations.literal: Qin asked to ransom him; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qin asked to ransom him; Wenxiang refused.

sentences.zh: 京再訴，文襄使監廚蒼頭薛豐洛杖之，曰：「更訴，當殺汝。

translations.literal: Jing appealed again; Wenxiang had the kitchen overseer Xue Fengluo beat him, saying, "Appeal again and I kill you."
translations.idiomatic: Jing appealed again; Xue Fengluo beat him and threatened death.

sentences.zh: 」京與其黨六人謀作亂。

translations.literal: Jing with six comrades plotted disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and six comrades plotted murder.

sentences.zh: 時文襄將受魏禪，與陳元康、崔季舒屏左右謀於北城東柏堂。

translations.literal: At that time Wenxiang was about to receive Wei's abdication; with Chen Yuankang and Cui Shushu he dismissed attendants and plotted in the eastern cypress hall of the north city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang was about to receive abdication and plotted with Chen Yuankang and Cui Shushu.

sentences.zh: 太史啟言宰輔星甚微，變不一月。

translations.literal: The court astronomer reported the minister star very faint; change within a month.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers said the minister star was faint; change within a month.

sentences.zh: 時京將進食，文襄卻之，謂人曰：「昨夜夢此奴斫我。

translations.literal: As Jing was about to bring food Wenxiang sent him away, telling others, "Last night I dreamed this slave cut me."
translations.idiomatic: As Jing brought food Wenxiang recalled a dream of being cut.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「急殺卻。

translations.literal: He also said, "Kill him at once."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Kill him at once."

sentences.zh: 」京聞之，置刀於盤下，冒言進食。

translations.literal: Jing heard it, placed a knife under the tray, and falsely said he brought food.
translations.idiomatic: Jing heard, hid a knife, and entered with food.

sentences.zh: 文襄見之，怒曰：「我未索食，何遽來？」

translations.literal: Wenxiang saw him and angrily said, "I did not ask for food; why do you come in haste?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang angrily said he had not asked for food.

sentences.zh: 京揮刀曰：「將殺汝！

translations.literal: Jing swung the knife and said, "I will kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: Jing swung the knife: "I will kill you!"

sentences.zh: 」文襄自投，傷足，入床下。

translations.literal: Wenxiang threw himself, wounding his foot, and went under the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang fell, wounded his foot, and crawled under the bed.

sentences.zh: 賊黨至，去床，因見弒，時年二十九。

translations.literal: The robber band arrived, pulled away the bed, and he was assassinated, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The band pulled away the bed and killed him, aged twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 秘不發喪。

translations.literal: Death was kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Death was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 明年正月辛酉，魏帝舉哀於太極東堂。

translations.literal: On the first day xinyou of the next year the Wei emperor mourned at the east hall of the Grand Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Next year on xinyou the emperor mourned at the Grand Ultimate east hall.

sentences.zh: 詔贈物八萬段，凶事依漢大將軍霍光、東平王蒼故事。

translations.literal: Edict bestowed eighty thousand bolts of goods; funeral followed Huo Guang and Prince Cang of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Edict bestowed eighty thousand bolts; funeral followed Huo Guang.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、使持節、相國、都督中外諸軍事、齊王璽紱，巉辌車、黃屋左纛、後部羽葆鼓吹、輕車介士，備九錫禮，謚曰文襄王。

translations.literal: Bestowed acting Yellow Battle-Ax, credentials, chancellor, command of all armies, Qi king's seal and ribbon, imperial carriage, yellow canopy left pennon, rear guard and whistling chariot, light chariot guard, full nine bestowals; posthumous title King Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He received the nine bestowals; posthumous title King Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 二月甲申，葬於義平陵之北。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the second month he was buried north of Yiping tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he was buried north of Yiping tomb.

sentences.zh: 天保初，追尊曰文襄皇帝，廟號世宗，陵曰峻成。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was further honored Emperor Wenxiang; temple name Shizong; tomb Juncheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianbao he became Emperor Wenxiang, temple Shizong, tomb Juncheng.

sentences.zh: 文襄美姿容，善言笑，談謔之際，從容弘雅。

translations.literal: Wenxiang had beautiful bearing and spoke well; in jest and banter he was easy and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang was handsome, witty, and refined in banter.

sentences.zh: 性聰警，多籌策，當朝作相，聽斷如流。

translations.literal: His nature was clever and alert with many stratagems; holding court as chancellor his decisions flowed like water.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and stratagem-rich, as chancellor he decided like flowing water.

sentences.zh: 愛士好賢，待之以禮，有神武之風焉。

translations.literal: He loved scholars and treated them with ritual; he had Shenwu's manner.
translations.idiomatic: He loved scholars and had Shenwu's manner.

sentences.zh: 然少壯氣猛，嚴峻刑法。

translations.literal: Yet in youth his spirit was fierce; his law was severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in youth he was fierce and his law severe.

sentences.zh: 高慎西叛，侯景南翻，非直本懷狼戾，兼亦有懼威略。

translations.literal: Gao Shen's western rebellion and Hou Jing's southern turn were not only their wolfish nature but also fear of his martial prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shen and Hou Jing rebelled from wolfish nature and fear of his prestige.

sentences.zh: 情欲奢淫，動乖制度。

translations.literal: His passions were extravagant and lewd; he often violated regulation.
translations.idiomatic: His passions were extravagant and often broke regulation.

sentences.zh: 嘗於宮西造宅，墻院高廣，聽事宏壯，亞太極殿。

translations.literal: He once built a mansion west of the palace; the walls and courtyards were high and broad, the reception hall grand, rivaling the Grand Ultimate Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He built a mansion west of the palace rivaling the Grand Ultimate Hall.

sentences.zh: 神武入朝，責之，乃止。

translations.literal: When Shenwu attended court he reproached him and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu reproached him and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 論曰：昔魏氏失馭，中原蕩析。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In old days Wei lost the reins and the central plains were torn apart.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Wei lost the reins and the central plains were torn apart.

sentences.zh: 齊神武爰從晉部，大號冀方。

translations.literal: Qi's Divine Martial arose from the Jin region and raised his standard in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's Divine Martial arose in Jin and raised his standard in Ji.

sentences.zh: 屢戰而翦凶徒，一麾以清京洛。

translations.literal: Again and again in battle he cut down vicious men; with one wave he cleared the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he cut down villains; with one wave he cleared the capital.

sentences.zh: 尊主匡國，功濟天下。

translations.literal: He honored the sovereign and righted the state; his merit saved the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He honored the sovereign and righted the state; his merit saved the realm.

sentences.zh: 既而魏武帝規避權逼，歷數既盡，適所以速關、河之分焉。

translations.literal: Then Emperor Wu of Wei plotted to escape coercive power; the mandate was spent, which is why the passes of Guan and He were soon divided.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Wu of Wei fled coercive power; the mandate was spent, and Guan and He were divided.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣膺霸道，威略昭著。

translations.literal: Wenxiang succeeded to overbearing rule; his martial prestige was manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang succeeded to overbearing rule; his prestige was manifest.

sentences.zh: 內除奸逆，外拓淮夷，擯斥貪殘，存情人物。

translations.literal: Within he removed traitors; without he extended the Huai; he drove off the greedy and cruel and cherished men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Within he removed traitors; without he reached the Huai; he cherished talent.

sentences.zh: 而志在峻法，急於禦下，於前王之德，有所未同。

translations.literal: Yet his aim lay in severe law and urgency in controlling subordinates; in the virtue of former kings he differed in part.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he aimed at severe law and harsh control; in virtue he differed from former kings.

sentences.zh: 蓋天意人心，好生惡殺，雖吉凶報應，未皆影響。

translations.literal: Surely heaven's heart and men's hearts love life and hate killing; though fortune and misfortune answer, they do not always shadow forth.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men love life and hate killing; fortune does not always answer at once.

sentences.zh: 總而論之，積善多慶。

translations.literal: Taken together, accumulating good brings many blessings.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, accumulating good brings many blessings.

sentences.zh: 然文襄之禍生所忽，蓋有由焉。

translations.literal: Yet Wenxiang's calamity arose from what he neglected; there was cause for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wenxiang's calamity arose from neglect; there was cause.
